Description: ATP binding cassette subfamily C member 4(ABCC4)
Curator's Note: Also known as leakytail. ATP- binding cassette transporter which transports prostaglandin E2 and other molecules across cellular membranes. Mutations in ABCC4 cause ciliogenesis defects. ABCC4-mediated PGE2 signalling acts through a ciliary G-protein-coupled receptor, EP4, to upregulate cAMP synthesis and increase anterograde IFT, thereby promoting ciliogenesis (PMID: 25173977). Zebrafish abcc4 mutants exhibited loss of connecting cilia and outer segment in photoreceptor cells, leading to mislocalization of opsins in the cell bodies of photoreceptors (PMID: 30685088). Specific missense associated with polydactyly in pigs (PMID: 32228435)
Involved in ciliation-related actin dynamics and LR patterning (PMID: 22684256). Asymmetrically expressed in both the node and left lateral plate mesoderm (LPM), similar to Nodal (PMID: 20487527)

ACE2 receptor protein robustly localizes within the membrane of the motile cilia of airway epithelial cells, which likely represents the initial or early subcellular site of SARS-CoV-2 viral entry during host respiratory transmission
Also known as ARP2. Target of miR-129-3p which regulates actin dynamics to regulate ciliation in cells and in zebrafish (PMID: 22684256)

Also known as tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α-converting enzyme (TACE). Metalloprotease, cleaves Notch receptor when glycosylated by GALNT11 to control formation of motile and non-motile cilia at the node. Heterotaxy gene (PMID: 24226769). Cleaves ACE2, found in respiratory cilia membrane (PMID: 15983030)

Description: ADAM metallopeptidase with thrombospondin type 1 motif 20(ADAMTS20)
Curator's Note: Secreted metalloproteases ADAMTS9 and ADAMTS20 have a non-canonical role in ciliary vesicle growth during ciliogenesis (PMID: 30814516)

Description: ADAM metallopeptidase with thrombospondin type 1 motif 9(ADAMTS9)
Curator's Note: Causes NPHP-related ciliopathy (PMID: 30609407). Has a non-canonical role in ciliary vesicle growth during ciliogenesis (PMID: 30814516)

GPR98. USH2C OMIM 602851. Mutation causes Usher syndrome type IIC

Description: anterior gradient 3, protein disulphide isomerase family member(AGR3)
Curator's Note: AGR3 expression is restricted to ciliated cells in the airway epithelium. Required for Regulation of Ciliary Beat Frequency in the Airway.

Mutated in Joubert syndrome (type 3) OMIM 608894, PMID:16453322. At mother centriole/basal body. Interacts with B9 complex of transition zone proteins including B9D1, B9D2, MKS1, TCTN1, TCTN2 PMID:22179047. Role in RAB8-dependent ciliary membrane targeting PMID:19625297.

Ultrastructural defects in 9+2 cilia, leading to PCD phenotype in mutant mice PMID:18776131. Role in ATP production to power ciliary beating. Reduced expression levels in PCD patients PMID:20537283. 1 single possibly pathogenic variant found in AK7 in 1 PCD patient PMID: 22801010. Homozygous missense mutation L673P in adenylate kinase 7 (AK7) leads to primary male infertility and multiple morphological anomalies of the flagella but not to primary ciliary dyskinesia. Mutations lead to spermatogenic failure in humans
Hydrocephalus due to dysfunctional motile cilia in KO mouse PMID: 21746835
Neddylation inhibitor MLN4924 suppresses cilia formation by modulating AKT1. Regulates a Rab11- Effector Switch Required for Ciliogenesis. PMID: 31204173
missense pathogenic variant in five families leads to ROSAH syndrome, an ocular multisystem autosomal dominant disorder.
Regulates ciliary length and disassembly of the primary cilium.

Ankrd26-/- mice display hyperphagia and have defects in primary cilia in regions of the central nervous system that control appetite and energy homeostasis (PMID: 24633808). With TALPID3 selectively orchestrates FBF1 localization and cilia gating (PMID: 32366837)

Description: ankyrin repeat and sterile alpha motif domain containing 3(ANKS3)
Curator's Note: Interacts with ANKS6 through sterile alpha motif (SAM), localised to renal cilia in mice
TMEM16A. Ca2+-activated Cl- channel .Regulates primary ciliogenesis.
Localises to cilia of olfactory epithelium.

Involved in ciliary targeting of rhodopsin and other proteins with VxPx motif. PMID:19153612. Targets proteins to cilia in association with ASAP1, RAB11 and RAB8 PMID:22983554. Dispensable for ciliogenesis
Patched1-ArhGAP36-PKA- Inversin axis determines the ciliary translocation of Smoothened for Sonic Hedgehog pathway activation.
Regulates cilia stability and development of outer segments in rod photoreceptor neurons.

Description: ADP ribosylation factor like GTPase 2 binding protein(ARL2BP)
Curator's Note: Needed for normal photoreceptor cilia doublets and outer segment structure.

interactor of RP2 PMID: 12417528 and PDEdelta PMID:10518933. Involved in trafficking of vesicles from the Golgi to the cilium PMID:20106869, especially; farnesylated cargo PMID:22002721 in association with PDEdelta and RPGR PMID:23559067; and myristoylated cargo in association with UNC119 and RP2 PMID:22085962 ARL3 Mutations Cause Joubert Syndrome by Disrupting Ciliary Protein Composition PMID: 30269812
Required for sperm flagellum formation. Bi-allelic Mutations in ARMC2 Lead to Severe Astheno-Teratozoospermia Due to Sperm Flagellum Malformations in Humans and Mice.
PCD with randomisation of body axis PMID: 23849778. Causes outer dynein arm defects in motile cilia PMID: 24203976
Localisation: Motile cilium axoneme and basal body

Curator's Note: Ciliopathy gene JBTS30 PMID:28625504. Interacts with coiled-coil domain containing 66 (CCDC66) and TOG array regulator of axonemal microtubules 1 (TOGARAM1) PMID: 32453716. Regulator of b- tubule length PMID: 30217954

Description: ArfGAP with SH3 domain, ankyrin repeat and PH domain 1(ASAP1)
Curator's Note: Targets proteins, such as rhodopsin and polycystin-1, to cilia in association with ARF4, RAB11 and RAB8 PMID:19153612, PMID:21775626. Provides a platform to regulate Arf4- and Rab11-Rab8-mediated ciliary cargo trafficking PMID:22983554
Major alpha-tubulin K40 acetyltransferase alphaTAT1. Promotes rapid ciliogenesis and efficient mechanosensation.

OFD1 at the centriolar satellites is rapidly degraded by autophagy upon serum starvation. In autophagy- deficient Atg5 or Atg3 null mouse embryonic fibroblasts, OFD1 accumulates at centriolar satellites, leading to fewer and shorter primary cilia and a defective recruitment of BBS4 (Bardet-Biedl syndrome 4) to cilia. MUtations cause spinocerebellar ataxia 25
Localisation: Cytoplasm. Discrete punctae along the ciliary axoneme and base of the ciliary axoneme

Curator's Note: Regulates ciliogenesis. Interacts with DYNLL1 (PMID: 25294941)
Controls Primary Cilia Formation to Allow for SHH- Triggered Granule Neuron Progenitor Proliferation.
ATP4a and canonical Wnt signaling are required in the epidermis for expression of foxj1, a transcriptional regulator of motile ciliogenesis.
kinase at the basal body of cilia. Phosphorylates HDAC6 to promote cilia disassembly

Mutated in Meckel-Gruber syndrome (type10) OMIM 611951 although mutations only found in 1 family PMID:21763481. Interacts with B9D2 and MKS1 at the transition zone PMID:22179047
Component of BBSome, implicated in BBS (BBS18) PMID: 24026985, PMID: 32055034
Required to maintain cilia orientation in multiciliated cells

Mutated in Bardet-Biedl syndrome (type 1) OMIM 209901 PMID: 12118255. Forms part of BBSome, mediates interaction with RABIN8 (RAB3IP), important for RAB8-mediated membrane protein trafficking PMID: 20603001, PMID:17574030, PMID:22072986

Mutated in Bardet-Biedl syndrome (type 12) OMIM 610683 PMID:17160889 Forms complex with other chaperonin-like BBS proteins to facilitate BBSome assembly PMID:20080638. At basal body of differentiating preadipocytes. Role in targeting of Wnt and Hh receptors to this cilium PMID:19190184.
Mutated in Bardet-Biedl syndrome (type 2) OMIM 606151 PMID:11285252. Forms part of BBSome, important for RAB8-mediated membrane protein trafficking PMID: 20603001, PMID:17574030, PMID:22072986
Mutated in Bardet-Biedl syndrome (type 4) OMIM 600374 PMID:11381270. Forms part of BBSome, important for RAB8-mediated membrane protein trafficking PMID: 20603001, PMID:17574030, PMID:22072986

Mutated in Bardet-Biedl syndrome (type 5) OMIM 603650 PMID:15137946. Forms part of BBSome, mediates binding to phospholipids, predominantly phosphatidylinositol 3- phosphate PMID: 20603001, PMID:17574030,
Mutated in Bardet-Biedl syndrome (type 7) OMIM 607590 PMID:12567324. Forms part of BBSome important for RAB8-mediated membrane protein trafficking PMID: 20603001, PMID:17574030, PMID:22072986

Mutated in Bardet-Biedl syndrome (type 7) OMIM 607968 PMID:16380913. Forms part of BBSome, important for RAB8-mediated membrane protein trafficking. Complex-organizing subunit of BBSome. PMID: 20603001, PMID:17574030, PMID:22072986

C11ORF74, interacts with the IFT-A complex via the IFT122 subunit and is accumulated at the distal tip in the absence of an IFT-A subunit IFT139, suggesting that at least a fraction of C11ORF74 molecules can be transported towards the ciliary tip by associating with the IFT-A complex, although its majority might be out of cilia at steady state (PMID: 30476139).

C2cd3 is an essential regulator of intracellular transduction of the Hedgehog signal (PMID: 19004860). Regulates primary cilium biogenesis, recruiting centriolar distal appendage proteins. C2cd3 is essential for ciliary vesicle docking (PMID: 24469809). Promotes centriolar elongation (PMID: 24997988)
Localisation: Basal Body. Centrioles and centriolar satellites in microtubules.

Description: calcium voltage-gated channel subunit alpha1 C(CACNA1C)
Curator's Note: CACNA1C, also called CaV1.2Serves as a modifier gene to cystic kidney phenotype. Plays an important role in Akt and Erk activities through cytosolic calcium and CaM kinase II. CaV1.2 might be a secondary calcium-permeable channel to the polycystins complex (PMID: 24925129). CaV1.2 expression is regulated through Wnt signaling and plays an essential sensory role in primary cilia for cellular homeostasis (PMID: 24700505).
Localisation: Primary cilia of epithelial cells. Cytoplasm of Pkd cells.

Curator's Note: It is involved in primary ciliogenesis in human cells and modulates actin polymerization, its depletion reduces the number of primary cilia without changing their length, suggesting it would be involved in cilia initiation rather than in cilia elongation. C2orf62 in association with TTC17 probably act on both motile and primary cilia formation (PMID, 24475127)
Localisation: Cytoplasm of spermatocytes, round and elongating spermatid, and Leydig cells. Nucleus and F-actin zone in cell membrane.

Description: chibby family member 1, beta catenin antagonist(CBY1)
Curator's Note: Inhibits beta-catenin-mediated transcriptional activation by competing with Tcf/Lef. Cby1 is required for recruitment of Arl13b to the primary cilium. Promotes Ahi1 localisation to the centriole and is probably important for assembly and function of transition zone components (PMID: 25103236). Cby1 may associate with membranes to promote the recruitment of FAM92 proteins for their higher-order assembly and subsequent membrane remodelling to promote ciliogenesis (PMID: 27528616). Because of its proximity to the membrane vesicle, it is possible that Cby proteins may be involved in targeting and/or attachment of the vesicles to the centriole, controlling intraflagellar transport and protein sorting of the ciliary membrane (PMID: 22911743).
Localisation: Distal end of mother centrioles and transition zone.

Curator's Note: Participates in microtubule stabilization that facilitates dynein arm attachment and ciliary motility (PMID: 28790179). Contributes to axonemal stability. A potential role, is to modify the doublet microtubule to provide a high affinity binding site for the docking complex and needed for dynein attachment (PMID: 25572396) Binds microtubules and stabilises them against cold depolymerization. It is also an outer dynein arm assembly factor (PMID: 31858719, PMID: 22581229)
Localisation: Axoneme. In zebrafish: Cytoplasm and axoneme.

Curator's Note: Subunit of the outer dynein arm (ODA) docking complex. It is responsible for axonemal microtubule attachment .

Ensures correct attachment of outer dynein arm (ODA) complexes to microtubules and is required for proper motile and non-motile functions, controls intraflagellar transport (IFT)- dependent dynein arm assembly and regulates primary cilia lenght in mammals. Required for the correct establishment of left-right asymmetry. When mutated causes PCD by disruption of the outer dynein arm docking complex formation (PMID: 25192045 )
Localisation: Outer dynein arm docking complex of motile cilia

Curator's Note: CCDC181 is a structural component of the axonemal structure of sperm flagella as well as motile cilia. It might be a component of the apparatus necessary for the generation of ciliary motility. C-terminal region interacts with microtubules of the axoneme and Hook1, acting as a linker protein for phosphoprotein phosphatase 1 (PP1) to tack the phosphatase to the axonemal structure of cilia and flagella. Pronostic factor for prostate cancer.
Localisation: Proximal portion of the ciliary axoneme. Basal half of motile cilia.

Curator's Note: CCDC39 regulates centriole/deuterosome amplification and multiciliogenesis. CCDC39/40 protein complex might define the binding site of radial spokes along peripheral microtubules and provide anchoring sites for inner dynein arms (PMID: 29317443). It is essential for assembly of inner dynein arms and the dynein regulatory complex (PMID: 21131972, PMID: 21131974)

CCDC40 is required for assembly of motile cilia. It is responsible for CCDC39 axonemal recruitment. It is important for cytoplasmic pre- assembly, axonemal targeting, and/or transport of axonemal components CCDC39, GAS11 and DNALI1. Necessary for assembly of inner dynein arms, the dynein regulatory complex and plays a role in the establishment of the left- right patterning (PMID: 21131974)

Organisation of spindle pole and centriolar satellite. It is involved in cilium formation, satellite organization, BBS4 recruitment to the primary cilium and ciliary trafficking. Overexpression induces formation of microtubule bundles, disruption of centriolar satellite organization and inhibits ciliogenesis (PMID: 28235840, PMID: 31582766). Interacts with ARMC9 and TOGORAM1 (PMID: 32453716). When mutated in dogs causes late onset retinal degeneration (PMID: 33273526)
Localisation: Centrosome, centriolar satellites and the primary cilium, along the axoneme.

Curator's Note: Centriole amplification mediated by deuterosome in multi-ciliated cells. Recruitment of Cep152 to the deuterosome required for centriole biogenesis.

Suppressor of ciliogenesis by acting simply as a passive physical barrier and by capping the growing ends of microtubules to prevent their elongation. Regulation the assembly of subdistal appendages (SDA) core components. Has a role in regulating centrosome duplication and separation (PMID: 26965371). Regulates the length of centrioles and prevents aberrant formation of primary cilia, components to a CP110 scaffold may be needed to facilitate depolymerization (PMID: 21620453). Studies suggest that CP110 might control discrete functions in the centrosome cycle and constitutes a set of controls that govern the switch from centriolar to basal body function (PMID: 17719545).

Roles in the folding of β- propeller proteins, such as Gβ1, in addition to its major target proteins, actin and tubulin. Interacts with chaperonin type BBSs, including BBSs 6, 10, and 12. Mutations in CCT2 could lead to genetic retinal diseases (PMID: 27645772)
Localisation: Basal body or the base of the connecting cilium

Curator's Note: Neuronal differentiation, ciliary formation or DNA damage repair. Studies suggest that is involved in neuronal connectivity and plasticity (PMID: 25850036). Potential activity in quiescent and differentiated cells, is recruited to the basal body of the primary cilium, where in complex with APC it negatively regulates ciliary length, by destabilizing axonemal microtubules (PMID: 25139956).
Localisation: Centrosome of postmitotic neurons, basal body.

Curator's Note: Specifically expressed in maturing multiciliated cells during the phase of centriole multiplication; it has been established the corresponding CDC20B protein as an essential regulator of centriole-deuterosome disengagement. Plays an essential and conserved role of in vertebrate multiciliogenesis. Function of promoting deuterosome
Localisation: Possible locations are: perideuterosomal region, multiciliary locus, deuterosome.

Curator's Note: Essential tip link component required for hair-cell mechanotransduction (PMID: 15057246). Encodes a protein of 3,354 amino acids with a single transmembrane domain and 27 cadherin repeats (PMID: 11138009). Studies suggest that Cdh23 are required for establishing and/or maintaining the proper organisation of the stereocilia bundle (PMID: 12121736).
Localisation: Near the tips of hair bundles.

Curator's Note: Interacts with Cyclin M (CycM), encoded by FAM58A to form an active protein kinase. CDK10/CycM is a key repressor of ciliogenesis through the regulation of RhoA and modulation of actin dynamics (PMID: 27104747). Important for normal regulation of ciliogenesis (PMID: 29130579).
Localisation: Base of primary cilia, basal body.

Curator's Note: Positively and negatively controls both ciliary length and the activity of the Hh pathway, regulates a broad array of processes at levels ranging from the subcellular to the organismal (PMID: 28817564).

Also known as p27Kip1. Multifunctional protein that plays crucial roles in cell architecture and migration by regulating rearrangements of the actin cytoskeleton and microtubules. p27Kip1 abrogation impairs one of the earliest events of ciliogenesis, docking of the Ehd1- associated preciliary vesicles to the distal appendages of the basal body (PMID: 32423824)

Description: cadherin EGF LAG seven-pass G-type receptor 2(CELSR2)
Curator's Note: Has been shown to be required for ciliogenesis (PMID: 27894351). Lack of cadherins Celsr2 and Celsr3 impairs ependymal ciliogenesis, leading to fatal hydrocephalus (PMID: 29420175), Whereas inactivation of Celsr2, Celsr3, Fzd3, and Vangl2 perturbs the organization of ependymal multicilia at the single-cell level (PMID: 25024228).

Description: cadherin EGF LAG seven-pass G-type receptor 3(CELSR3)
Curator's Note: Lack of cadherins Celsr2 and Celsr3 impairs ependymal ciliogenesis, leading to fatal hydrocephalus (PMID: 29420175), controls the function of ependymal cilia (PMID: 29327175), Whereas inactivation of Celsr2, Celsr3, Fzd3, and Vangl2 perturbs the organization of ependymal multicilia at the single-cell level (PMID: 25024228).

Acts as a scaffold for the cilium disassembly complex, which includes Nde1, Aurora A, and OFD1, which is recruited to the ciliary base for timely cilium disassembly, plays a role in NPC proliferation, cilia formation, controlling the cilium axoneme and BB structure, regulates centriole duplication and elongation (PMID: 30626697). Promotes the extension of the centriolar cylinder, presumably via its ability to recruit tubulin to the nascent structure, studies propose that functions as a scaffold for tubulin addition (PMID: 19481458).

Has an important role in regulating microtubule length in cilia by facilitating tubulin addition to ciliary microtubules and might also be involved in regulating other factors, possibly by interacting with Nek1. Cep104 is involved in the stabilization of the ciliary axoneme or in cilia formation and elongation, mutations cause ciliopathies (PMID: 28017521). Regulates ciliary assembly by interacting with centriolar proteins that suppress cilia formation, detaches from these proteins at the onset of cilia formation and moves to the tip of the nascent cilium (PMID: 23970417).

It encodes a subdistal appendage protein that regulates TGF-β/bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) signaling and RAB11 trafficking at the primary cilium. It has no major effect on centrosome structure but leads to increased ciliation frequency (PMID: 29514088).

Contributor to ciliogenesis in certain tissues in the developing vertebrate embryo, involved in assembling the cilium and in determination of the length of the axoneme (PMID: 19254375). The Atoh1- Cep131-CS integrity axis would act as a gatekeeper during GNPs’ ciliogenesis, as it would provide cells an essential machinery (i.e., the CS) for building the primary cilia (PMID: 30695697).

Promotes and restricts transition zone (TZ) assembly before ciliogenesis. Interacts with core TZ components CEP290 and mediates their association with MTs. Loss of CEP162 arrests ciliogenesis at the stage of TZ assembly; gain of CEP162 at cilia tips promotes ectopic assembly of TZ components

Assembly of primary cilia and promotes vesicular docking and trafficking that initiates cilia membrane biogenesis (PMID: 17954613, PMID: 23253480). CEP164 promotes accumulation of GTP-Rab8 at the centrosome, providing a molecular link connecting the M-centriole to components of the machinery that initiate ciliary membrane biogenesis (PMID: 23253480). Recruitment of active tau tubulin kinase 2 (TTBK2) to centrioles, leading to removal of CP110 and recruitment of intraflagellar

Required for anchoring the subdistal appendages (SDA) complex in the centrifuge to the cytoplasmic microtubule network. It is an FHDC1 buinding protein to keep this connection (PMID: 29742020). Recruits microtubule-depolymerizing factor KIF2A to disassemble cilium (PMID: 31197141).

Recruitment of ciliary vesicles to the centrioles during early ciliogenesis, which suggest it is a regulator for membrane trafficking pathways . CEP19 recruits and associates with RABL2 to the basal body, promoting cilia assembly via its interactions with the FT-B complex (PMID: 28659385). CEP19-RABL2B complex plays a critical role as a regulator to initiate intraflagellar transport (PMID: 28625565, PMID: 28428259).
Localisation: Basal body: subdistal appendages of mother centriole.

Curator's Note: Interact with proteins implicated in rhodopsin trafficking (NEK2 and NINL). Rrecruitment of several proteins to centriole proximal ends, including Girdin (Girders of actin filaments) and proteins that associate with the distal region of the mother centriole (NEK2, ninein, CEP170, p150glued and KIF2A) (PMID: 30421101). C-NAP1 anchores rootletin filaments that hold

Assembly and stabilisation of the primary cilium as well as centrosomal function (PMID: 30478281, PMID: 22563985). Interacts with a centriolar satellite protein PCM-1 and is implicated in molecular pathways related to BBS4 function. CEP250 binds PCM- 1 and are involved in ciliary targeting of Rab8 required to promote ciliogenesis. Interacts with components of both dynein and kinesin motor machineries (PMID: 18772192). Regulation of intracellular protein trafficking by association with microtubule-based transport protein RPGR (PMID: 16632484). CEP250 plays an important role in the formation and stabilisation of the primary cilium as well as centrosomal function, stabilises the linkage of axoneme microtubules to the ciliary membrane to maintain the integrity of the ciliary diffusion barrier. CEP290 is critical for positioning the molecular components that are necessary for correct processing of Shh signalling in the primary cilium (PMID: 30478281)
Localisation: Centriolar satellites. Centrosome and basal body. Y-link junctions of the ciliary transition zone

Curator's Note: Regulation of tubulin glutamyl posttranslational modifications by mediating ciliary transport of TTLL6 between the basal body and cilium, therefore, it is also required for localising TTLL6 to the cilium. CEP41 is also involved in ciliary structural formation and motility through glutamylation and its loss of CEP41 has been identified as a cause of Joubert syndrome (PMID: 22246503). CEP41 regulates cilia disassembly and angiogenesis through AURKA activation by modulating axonemal tubulin glutamylation (PMID: 31885126)

Regulation of the centrosomal localisation of γ-tubulin complex components, CG- NAP, and Kiz. Cep72 provides centrosomal microtubule-nucleation activity and has critical roles in spindle-pole formation, which is needed for proper tension generation between sister chromatids during mitosis (PMID: 19536135). Recruitment of Cep290 to centriolar satellites by interaction with PCM1. Regulates ciliary recruitment and relocalisation of BBS4 from centriolar satellites to primary cilia during ciliogenesis, which affects assembly and recruitment of the BBSome (PMID: 22767577).

Recruitment of distal appendages proteins like SCLT1 and CEP89 (PMID: 23348840). CEP83 phosphorylation mediated by TTBK2, regulates docking of membrane vesicles to mother centrioles, promoting CP110 removal and cilia initiation. Mutation have been associated with infantile nephronophthisis (PMID: 31455668).

Also calles CEP13 and CCDC123. Assembly of primary cilium and membrane docking (PMID: 23348840). It interacts with the centriolar satellite proteins PCM-1 and OFD1 for cilia formation, and with Cep290 for the recruitment of membranes to the centrosome. CEP123 is required for the formation of a ciliary vesicle at the distal end of the mother centriole during primary ciliogenesis (PMID: 23789104)
Localisation: Distal appendages of mother centriole, centriolar satellite.

Curator's Note: Synthesis and accumulation of CETN2 is required for centriole duplication (PMID: 12176356). Regulation of primary ciliogenesis through controlling CP110 levels and localisation (PMID: 25753040). Stabilisation of connecting cilium axoneme structure. CETN2 is required for photoreceptor survival by regulating SPATA7 CC localization, distal connecting cilium/axoneme microtubule stability, and outer segment disc orientation (PMID: 30647131)

CETN3 is also required for photoreceptor survival by regulating SPATA7 CC localization, distal connecting cilium/axoneme microtubule stability, and outer segment disc orientation (PMID: 30647131). CETN3 restrains centriole assembly by inhibiting Mps1 kinase activity at centrosomes and phosphorylation of both the specific substrate CETN2 (PMID: 26354417)

Also called Flattop.Required cilia formation. Regulator for BB docking and positioning in mono- and multiciliated cell types that acquire planar cell polarity. Fltp interacts with Dlg3 to surround the basal body and anchor this organelle asymmetrically to the apical cortex (PMID: 25296022)
Localisation: Next to basal body, microtubules plus end,adjacent to the apical plasma membrane

Curator's Note: Interacts with tubulin and CEP350, it targets proteins to the centrosome and is therefore required for ciliogenesis. Downstream efector of FOXJ1 that acts during spermiogenesis potentially suppressing the formation of supernumerary axonemes and ensures a correct ultrastructur (PMID: 27965440)
Also called C15orf26. Studies in zebrafish suggest it is essential for cilia motility (PMID: 24094744)

Also known as C21orf59 or kur) Mutated in primary ciliary diskinesia and regulates dynein arm assembly required for motile cilia function (PMID: 24094744). Involved in cilia- associated developmental processes, recruitment of outer dynein arms required for initiating cilia motility. Studies suggest it has a role in the establishment of cilia polarity (PMID: 26904945)

(c11orf70) Involved in the cytoplasmic assembly, maturation, intraflagellar transport (IFT)-dependant assembly of axonemal dyneins required for cilia motility in multiciliated cells. Plays a role within protein folding and trafficking pathways required for the cytoplasmic preassembly of dynein arm motors and subsequent import into the motile ciliary axoneme (PMID: 29727692, PMID: 29727693)
Interacts with Arl3 and may regulate its ciliary localisation and function (PMID: 26455799)

Formation of flagellar axonemes during spermatogenesis. Contains WD repeat domains, which are highly enriched in the intraflagellar transport proteins of sperm flagella (PMID: 28552195). Essential for beating, but not rotating left-right organiser (LRO) or immotile cilia. Involved in the regulation of the beating frequency of tracheal cilia (PMID: 31884020)

Hemizygous mutations in CFAP47 can induce X-linked multiple morphological abnormalities of the flagella and asthenoteratozoospermia in humans and mice. Expressed in spermatozoa, but exact localisation not known (PMID: 33472045)

Also called WDR16. Wdr16 can be considered a differentiation marker of kinocilia‐bearing cells. In the brain, it appears to be functionally related to water homeostasis or osmoregulation. It might be speculated that Wdr16 has some role in cilia-mediated cell polarity (PMID: 17394468). CFAP52 protein has been proposed to play a role in cilia-related signal transduction processes and

Also called CCDC11. Assembly and function of primary and motile cilia, providing recruitment sites for proteins destined for the centrosome and cilium. Involved in left-right patterning and maintaining centriolar satellite organization of PCM- 1 and Cep290 at centriolar satellites (PMID: 26538025).
Member of C1d complex. CFAP54 is required C1d assembly mechanisms, therefor, it is necessary for proper assembly and motility of mammalian cilia and flagella. Role in spermatogenesis (PMID: 26224312)

Also known as WDR65. Required for the asymmetric targeting of a subset of inner dynein arms in Chlamydomonas. In normal human nasal epithelial cells, CFAP57 localizes throughout the ciliary axoneme. Homozygous nonsense variant found in one PCD case (PMID: 32764743)
Localisation: Throughout the ciliary axoneme in human nasal epithelial cilia

Curator's Note: Biallelic mutations in CFAP65 lead to severe asthenoteratospermia due to acrosome hypoplasia and multiple malformations of the sperm flagella (PMID: 31413122; PMID: 31501240; PMID: 31571197)

CFAP69 is necessary for flagellum assembly/stability. Mutations cause multiple morphological abnormalities of the flagella and primary male infertility (PMID: 29606301). Regulates olfactory transduction kinetics in the olfactory sensory neurons of mice (PMID: 28495971)
Regulator component of the outer dynein arm in motile cilia and flagella, regulating ciliary motility and length (PMID: 30158508)
Localisation: Ciliary axoneme at the base of outer dynein arm.

Curator's Note: Also known as ICK. Regulator of ciliary transport through regulation of BBS proteins and IFT-B localisation. Loss of ICK causes accumulation of IFT-A, IFT-B, and BBSome components at the ciliary tips. It is a Kif3a kinase essential for proper ciliogenesis (PMID: 24797473, PMID: 25243405). Involved in the negative control of ciliary length; abnormal ICK function results in the mislocalisation of key mediators for Shh (PMID: 24853502, PMID: 25243405). Anterograde tafficking of CILK is essential for retrograde IFT (PMID: 32732286)

Description: cell proliferation regulating inhibitor of protein phosphatase 2A(CIP2A)
Curator's Note: Promotes primary cilia disassembly through the activation of Aurora A kinase. Depletion increases ciliated cells and cilia length in retinal pigment epithelium cells. CIP2A enhances NEK2 kinase activity to facilitate centrosome separation. It plays a role in c-MYC stabilization and metabolic reprogramming toward the glycolytic pathway (PMID: 29491003)

Responsible for the Na+ and H2O permeability of the tight junctions and despite being a ciliary protein, it is not necessary for ciliogenesis. Claudin-2 is associated to acetylated α-tubulin (PMID: 22143774)

Regulation of localization of Pcdh15a to the apical aspect of hair cells, contributing to the assembly and/or function of the mechanotransduction apparatus. Clarin-2 constitutes a docking site for proteins destined for the cilium and may be a modulator during late ciliogenesis. Modulation of vesicle recycling, distribution and/or assembly of diverse components necessary for normal hair cell function. Mutations in the clarin-1 gene are associated with Usher syndrome type 3 (PMID: 25365995). Vesicle transport and stereocilia/synaptic development and/or maintenance (PMID: 19539019)
Localisation: Stereocilia and below the cuticular plate in the transition zone ciliary subcompartment. Microtubules in UB/OC-1 cells.

Curator's Note: Subunit of the cyclic nucleotide-gated (Cng) channel localised to the outer segment. Mutations in Cnga1 which have been associated with retinitis pigmentosa in humans (PMID: 25319694)
Localisation: Outer segment plasma membrane. Rab11-positive recycling endosomes (mediated by Numb).

Curator's Note: Principal subunit of heteromeric olfactory CNG channels and homomeric CNGA2 channels in nonmotile cilia on olfactory sensory neurons (ORNs). N-terminus of CNGA2 are necessary for PIP3 regulation. In absence of CNGB1, it does assemble and form functional heteromeric channels in ORNs (PMID: 17032767)

It endows the olfactory CNG channel with a variety of biophysical properties tailored to the specific requirements of olfactory transduction and is required for ciliary targeting of the olfactory CNG channel. Cooperation in mediating feedback modulation by Ca2+-CaM (PMID: 16980309). Key regulators of disk size by mediating a physical connection between disk rims and the OS plasma membrane Loss of Cngb1 disruptes links between the disk and plasma membranes (PMID: 23178122)

Also known as JBTS17. Most common mutated gene in Joubert syndrome and the related oral-facial-digital syndrome type VI (OFDVI). (PMID: 29321670). JBTS17 contributes to mitotic progression by interacting with LIS1, its depletion disrupts chromosome alignment and spindle pole orientation, resulting in mitotic delay (PMID: 31004438). JBTS17 acts upstream of NPHP1 in the assembly of the NPHP1-4-8 complex in the cilia transition zone, it is required for efficient SHH signaling and for establishing cell polarity (PMID: 25877302).

Epithelial polarity, tight junction formation and ciliogenesis. CRB3-CLPI isoform interacts with importin β-1 to be delivered to spindle poles during cell division and ciliogenesis, and this delivery may be important for centrosome maintenance (PMID: 17646395). It modulates intraflagellar transport and cilia elongation together with Par3/Par6/aPKC polarity complex (PMID: 28882989, PMID: 15324661)
Localisation: Cilium, cilia membrane and a membrane compartment at the mitotic spindle poles

Curator's Note: Structural component of the ciliary rootlet. Coiled-coil interaction in the extended α- helical rod domain of rootletin is a key feature in rootlet formation (PMID: 12427867). Interaction between the rootlet and intermediate filaments may contribute substantially to the role as support structure for the cillium. Candidate gene for human retinal degeneration (PMID: 15870283). interacts with the large coiled-coil protein, C-NAP1, to connect parental centrioles and maintain centrosome cohesion. Positive regulation of ciliogenesis (PMID: 23070519). CHE-10/rootletin maintains ciliary integrity by modulating the assembly, motility, and flux of IFT particles, which are critical for axoneme length control; and is essential for stabilizing ciliary transition zones and basal bodies (PMID: 24094853)
Localisation: Rootlets. Proximal ends of centrioles in nonciliated cells

Description: centrosome and spindle pole associated protein 1(CSPP1)
Curator's Note: CSPP proteins may be involved in cytoskeletal organization and for correct localisation of NPHP8 to the tip of the basal body that is forming the transition zone (PMID: 20519441). Interacts with CEP104 at microtubules for the regulation of axoneme length and Hedgehog pathway stimulation (PMID: 31412255). CSPP1 is required for localization of axonemal proteins, such as ARL13B and AC3; loss of CSPP1 is a cause of Joubert syndrome (PMID: 24360808).
Localisation: Transition zone, basal body and axoneme of primary cilia (centrioles and midbody of cycling cells; centrioles and cilia axoneme in resting cells)

Curator's Note: Component of the intercentrosomal linker and a key regulator of mitotic centrosome separation (PMID: 18086858). Required for Kupffer’s vesicle (KV) and cilia formation, and organ laterality. Ctnnb1/2 activity in dorsal forerunner cells is required for cilia formation by controlling the expression of a set of transcription factors (PMID: 22535411). Interacts with TCF family members, activating Wnt target genes (PMID: 15852005). Ciliary
Localisation: Centrosome: proximal and distal regions of the centriole, and between centrioles.

Curator's Note: Mutated in M3 syndrome. Fibroblast with CUL7 homozygous mutations showed significantly fewer cilia than wild-type. Nevertheless, cilia could be restored by overexpression of wild type CUL7, suggesting that 3M syndrome is indeed a ciliopathy (PMID: 27173435).

Deconjugation of the polyubiquitin chain from centrosomal protein Cep70 and promotes ciliogenesis by inhibiting the tubulin deacetylase activity of HDAC6. Regulation of the docking of basal bodies to the apical plasma membrane. CYLD is also required for proper organization of basal bodies and axenomes (PMID: 25342559). CYLD may control the centriolar satellites proteostasis by preventing the proteasomal degradation of PCM1 (PMID: 31067453).

Cystin may not involved in a ciliogenic pathway, but would rather play a novel role in ciliary function. It bounds to the axonemal membrane and may function as part of a molecular scaffold that stabilizes microtubule assembly within the ciliary axoneme (PMID: 11854326).
Localisation: Ciliary membrane, axoneme, primary apical cilia.

Curator's Note: Functional role in ciliary signaling . DCDC2 overexpression increases ciliary length and enhances the Kif3a mediated translocation of Smo to the cilium, resulting in overactivation of the Shh pathway in neurons (PMID: 21698230). Regulation of microtubule nucleation, stability and length in hair cells (PMID: 25601850). Overexpression inhibits β- catenin-dependent Wnt signaling (PMID: 25557784)
Localisation: Neurites, ciliary axoneme, cytoplasm, cellular microtubule network.

Curator's Note: Mutations in DDX59 cause an autosomal-recessive form of orofaciodigital syndrome, nevertheless, normal ciliogenesis is observed.

Promotes both actin polymerization and EB1- dependent microtubule (MT) stability, both actin nucleating and microtubule-stabilizing properties of DIAPH1 are important for their cilia functions. Depletion of DIAPH1 decreased ciliogenesis, cilia length, and reduced trafficking within cilia. Conversely, targeting of DIAPH1 specifically to the

Regulation of the formation and/or maintenance of primary cilia, and establish subtype-specific targeting of dopamine receptors to the ciliary surface. Interacts with centriolar and ciliary components (PMID: 20531939). Ciliogenesis and intraflagellar transport regulation through MIPT3 interaction. DISC1 is involved in plus-end and minus-end microtubular transport (PMID: 28125008)
Localisation: Near nucleus, basal body, transition zone, microtubules, and mitochondria

Description: DLEC1 cilia and flagella associated protein(DLEC1)
Curator's Note: Interacts with BBS protein complex subunits, as well as α- and β-tubulin. Expression enhances primary cilia formation and cilia length in A549 lung adenocarcinoma cells. Elongating spermatids in Dlec1-/- mice show head deformation, a shortened tail, and abnormal manchette organization. These phenotypes were similar to those of various intraflagellar transport (IFT)-associated gene-deficient sperm (PMID: 33144677)

Preassembly protein that functions a link between the early- and late-phase complexes requiered for proper assembly of the IDA and ODA in motile cilia, providing a mechanism for amplification for rapid preassembly, allowing simultaneous fabrication of thousands of motor units for delivery to axoneme microtubules during ciliogenesis (PMID: 29358401). Required for dynein heavy chains folding (PMID: 22387996)

Needed for assembly of multiple axonemal inner and outer dynein arms into complexes beefore being transported into cilia, critical for nodal cilia motility. Loss prevents correct assembly of inner and outer dynein arms, abolishing motility of respiratory cilia and giving rise to classical primary ciliary dyskinesia with defective left- right organ asymmetry and male infertility (PMID:

Cytoplasmic axonemal dynein assembly factor (DYX1C1) that probably acts together with DNAAF2 at an early step of cytoplasmic ODA and IDA assembly (PMID: 23872636). Involved in ciliary and basal body biogenesis (PMID: 23650548)
Preassembly and/or stability of both outer and inner axonemal dynein arms, required for ciliary motility. Interacts with DNAI2 in the initial step of outer dynein arms assembly (PMID: 25232951)

Also known as PIH1D3. Involved in the cytoplasmatic preassembly of both outer (ODA) and inner (IDA) dynein arms of cilia and sperm flagella. Loss-of-function mutations cause X-linked primary ciliary dyskinesia with ciliary and sperm immotility in humans (PMID: 28041644, PMID: 28176794). Interacts with Dnaic2 (ODA IC2), Hsp70 and Hsp90, and may be required to maintain the stability of the IC1–IC2 complex (PMID: 24421334).Mutations lead to absence of outer and inner
Localisation: Cytoplasm in sperm, trans-Golgi network in ciliated epithelia cells

Curator's Note: Formation of the inner dynein arms; its absence is deleterious for the organization and biogenesis of the axoneme. Knockout causes asthenozoospermia and and respiratory disease due to decrease in the beat frequency of tracheal cilia (PMID: 11371505)
Localisation: Inner surface of the peripheral microtubule doublets of the motile axoneme.

Curator's Note: Component of outer dynein arm (PMID:15937072, PMID: 11175280, PMID: 29843777). Heterotaxy candidate gene, involved in left-right patterning regulaton by affecting the notochord. Participates in protozoan flagellar motility (PMID: 29843777)
Localisation: Motile cilia axoneme, attached to the peripheral microtubule doublets

Curator's Note: Encodes a ciliary outer dynein arm protein. Required for bending of the proximal ciliary region during the effective and recovery strokes of the ciliary beat cycle. Mutations are a common cause of primary ciliary dyskinesia and situs inversus (PMID: 26909801, PMID: 29467202, PMID: 12142464)
Component of axonemal inner dynein arm-f, essential for ciliary beat (PMID: 30060180). DNAH2 mutation can cause severe sperm flagella defects that damage sperm motility (PMID: 30811583).

Component of ciliary outer dynein arms, mutations can cause primary ciliary dyskinesia (PMID: 30471717, PMID: 11062149). Cilia with complete axonemal DNAH5 deficiency are immotile (PMID: 15750039). Essential for correct assembly of DNAI2 in type 1 and 2 ODA complexes (PMID: 18950741)
Localisation: Along entire axoneme in respiratory cells. Reduced in distal part of the cilia when DNAH9 is mutated. In sperm cells, localises only to the proximal part of the flagellum.

Curator's Note: Putative inner dynein arm component. Required for ciliogenesis and motile cilia function mediating airway clearance and left/right patterning. Mutations can cause heterotaxy and ciliary dysfunction similar to primary ciliary dyskinesia by disruption of cilia ultrastructure (PMID: 26918822)

Component of ciliary outer dynein arms and is required in cilia motility and ODA stability. In individuals with pathogenic variants in DNAH11, DNAH9 can reside in the place of DNAH11. Mutations confer a loss of ODAs in the distal portion of the ciliary axoneme and affects the ciliary beat pattern (PMID: 30471717). Essential in distal axonemal assembly and docking of ODAs type 2, which occurs via direct interaction of DNAH9 with the docking complex protein CCDC114 (PMID: 30471718)
Localisation: Distal region of ciliary axonemes in respiratory cells. In sperm cells, it localises the entire length of the sperm tail.

Curator's Note: Axonemal outer dynein intermediate-chain protein. Mutations result in primary ciliary dyskinesia with situs solitus or situs inversus (PMID: 11231901). DNAI and DNAI2 form a complex essential for the stability of both proteins during early stages of outer dynein arms assembly (PMID: 29113992)

Outher dynein arm intermediate chain protein. DNAI and DNAI2 form a complex essential for the stability of both proteins during early stages of outer dynein arms assembly (PMID: 29113992). Essential for axonemal assembly of the ODA heavy chains DNAH5 and DNAH9 (PMID:

Description: DnaJ heat shock protein family (Hsp40) member B13(DNAJB13)
Curator's Note: Role in the proper formation and function of ciliary and flagellar axonemes in humans, preserving the integrity of the central complex of motile cilia and flagella (PMID: 27486783)
Localisation: Co-localises with α- tubulin along the length of cilia and flagella. Radial spokes, annulus during spermiogenesis.

Curator's Note: Encodes an outer dynein arm light chain protein. Candidate gene for primary ciliary dyskisenia. Regulatory function for DNAH5 activity in outer dynein arms of sperm flagella, respiratory cilia, and ependymal cilia (PMID: 15845866). Necessary for the function of the cilia that produce the nodal flow essential for the determination of left-right asymmetry (PMID: 21496787)
Localisation: Associated with A- tubule of the outer doublets

Curator's Note: Light chain of axonemal inner dynein arms protein. Formation of complexes with the dynein heavy chains, actin, and caltractin/centrin molecules required in ciliary motility (PMID: 9284741)

Description: deleted in primary ciliary dyskinesia homolog (mouse)(DPCD)
Curator's Note: Reported situs inversus, hydrocephalus, and suppurative rhinosinusitis in Dpcd/Poll–/– mice (PMID: 21746835). Potential role in the formation or function of ciliated cells. Mutations in DPCD may be responsible for PCD (PMID: 14630615)
Neuronal protein that guides neurite growth. Also called CRMP-2, is a GSK-3β substrate and a microtubule- binding protein. Required for primary cilium biogenesis.
Localisation: Centrosome/Basal body. Primary cillium during cillium formation.

Curator's Note: Structural component of the nexin-dynein regulatory complex (N-DRC), critical for regulation of the dynein motors. Its integrity is essential for the regulation of ciliary beat. Mutations are a cause for an autosomal recessive variant of primary ciliary dyskinesia (PMID: 23354437). DRC1 and DRC2 form a subcomplex in the cytoplasm prior to assembly into the axoneme. DRC1 and
Localisation: Cytoplasm, axoneme. N-DRC starting from the linker domain, spanning across the base plate, and ending near the hole on the inner junction.

Curator's Note: Component of N-DRC, important in flagellar motility (PMID: 27261005). Studies suggest it is required for other N-DRC components to assemble into the N-DRC. Its location suggests that DRC3 could be important for transducing regulatory signals from the radial spokes through the base plate of the N-DRC to the dynein motor (PMID: 25564608).
Localisation: Axoneme. L1 projection of the nexin linker region of N-DRC that connects to inner dynein arm.

Curator's Note: Central linker subunit that helps connect the N-DRC to the outer dynein arms. Loss of DRC7 causes defects in sperm storage and fertility (PMID: 31659045). Essential for the correct assembly of the N-DRC and flagella; stability of the N-DRC is essential for proper axoneme elongation. DRC7 is essential to localize DRC5 in the correct place, and that DRC5 regulates flagellar motility (PMID: 31961863)
Localisation: Entire axoneme. Central region of the N-DRC linker including the outer dynein/inner dynein linker.

Curator's Note: Role in motile ciliary beating in ependymal cells by regulation of catecholamines. Mediation of cellular responses to distinct endogenous catecholamines, which suggests that primary cilia play a fundamental role in enhancing the selectivity of integrated catecholamine signaling (PMID: 23936473)

Ciliary mechanosensory protein in vascular endothelial cells. DR5 activation increases cilia length in a concentration-dependent manner and restores cilia function in the mutant cells (PMID: 21709211)

Essential for the docking of basal bodies to the apical plasma membrane through the activation of the Rho GTPase. DVL and Rho are required for the planar polarization of basal bodies that underlies directional beating of cilia (PMID: 18552847). DVL is a central component of WNT signalling. PTEN regulates multicilia formation and cilia disassembly by controlling the phosphorylation of DVL (PMID: 26399523).

Also known as DHC2. Component of interflagellar transport dynein assembly complex, that regulates retrograde trafficking from the ciliary tip to the base (PMID: 30429209, PMID: 9971742). Directly involved in the contacts and translocation of the dynein complex along microtubules via its large motor domain (PMID: 19442771). Role in Golgi
Localisation: Golgi, axoneme, peri- basal body pool

Curator's Note: Component of the dynein‐2 microtubule motor protein complex with a role in the retrograde transport of cargo in primary cilia. Mutations have been associated to Ellis- van Creveld syndrome (PMID: 28857138, PMID: 26130459). Essential for dynein-2 complex stability, cilium function, Hedgehog regulation, skeletogenesis and primary cilia length (PMID: 26077881),
Localisation: Cytoplasm, centrosomes, around basal body, transition zone.

Curator's Note: Control of retrograde intraflagellar trafficking of ciliary proteins through interaction with WDR34 and ciliogenesis by serving as dynein-1 subunits (PMID: 25294941, PMID: 30649997).

Required for the correct assembly of the dynein complex. It has been implicated in controlling its association with cargo molecules (PMID: 25205765). Component of the WDR34 subcomplex (DYNLL1/DYNLL2 and DYNLRB1/DYNLRB2), crucial for dynein-2 function in retrograde ciliary protein trafficking (PMID: 30649997). DYNLRB1 is essential for dynein-mediated axonal transport of lysosomes, late endosomes and signaling endosomes (PMID: 32088381)
Component of the WDR34 subcomplex (DYNLL1/DYNLL2 and DYNLRB1/DYNLRB2), crucial for dynein-2 function in retrograde ciliary protein trafficking (PMID: 30649997, PMID: 32088381).

Also known as TCTEX1. Light chain subunit of cytoplasmic dynein. Regulation of ciliary resorption and S-phase entry. Tctex-1 is not required for ciliogenesis, but is critical for cilium disassembly (PMID: 21394082). Component of dynein-2. Modulator of cilia length control; depletion is associated to increased cilia length (PMID: 21700358).
Localisation: Axoneme, transition Zone between primary cilia and basal body.

Curator's Note: Mediates membrane/basal- body interactions, functions in basal-body maturation and transition zone organisation. Required to recruit Fam92 and Cby at the basal body distal end, allowing proper transition zone assembly; both DZIP and FARM92 control the distal elongation of basal bodies and docking to the plasma membrane (PMID: 31821146, PMID: 32491167). Mediates the assembly of the BBSome-Dzip1-PCM1 complex in the centriolar satellites for ciliary translocation of the BBSome (PMID: 27979967). Necessary for recruiting IFT machinery to the distal appendages of the mother centrioles and for bridging IFT88 to the cargo that contains GLI3. Positive regulator of Shh (PMID: 23955340). Together with GSK3β and Rab8, DZIP1 co- regulates ciliogenesis by promoting ciliary membrane assembly (PMID: 25860027).
Localisation: Transition zone, mother centrioles, centriolar satellites, cytoplasm, nucleus.

Curator's Note: Mediation of the transcriptional responses of Multicilin. Forms apical cytoplasmic organizing centres for multiciliogenesis, recruitment and accumulation of early regulators of centriole biogenesis to allow assembly and nucleation of deuterosomes (PMID: 28675157).
Localisation: Nucleus, cytoplasm (beneath primary cillium and in small foci or granules).

Curator's Note: Positive regulation of Hedgehog pathway. Adaptor to link the EVC-EVC2 complex to IQCE (PMID: 24582806).
Localisation: Base of cilia in the EvC zone

Curator's Note: Also known as RIB72. Encondes a non-ion channel protein myoclonin1. Modulates TRP mechanosensitive calcium channels. Mutations are linked to juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (PMID: 30810526). Regulation of Wnt signaling (PMID: 26783883). Interacts functionally with the system of linkages that hold the doublet microtubules and limits microtubule sliding (PMID:

Suppression of ciliogenesis by directly phosphorylating the deubiquitinase USP8, which stabilises the trichoplein-Aurora A pathway (PMID: 29472535) and through the MEK and ERK pathway (PMID: 31430961). Contributes to cell cycle progression through inhibition of ciliogenesis (PMID: 29472535).
Localisation: Golgi, plasma membrane, clathrin coated vesicle membrane, lipid raft, cell junctions
Ciliary pocket membrane, membrane tubules, pre-ciliary vesicles and distal appendage vesicles. Centrosome in the absence of Rab8

Curator's Note: Function in early ciliogenesis by causing mother centriole reorganisation. Regulation of membrane tubulation required for ciliary vesicle formation from smaller distal appendage vesicles. EHD1 and EHD3 bind to the Rab8 effector MICAL-L1 and affect membrane tubulo-vesicle formation and scission (PMID: 25686250).
Localisation: Ciliary pocket membrane, membrane tubules, pre-ciliary vesicles and distal appendage vesicles.

Curator's Note: Required for patterning the left/right axis in vertebrates. Mutations in humans cause situs inversus (PMID: 29257953). Potential role as a Ca2+ sensor that participates in the regulation of mammalian flagellar bending (PMID: 29733335, PMID: 15385169).
Localisation: Motile cilia, axoneme.Near to developing acrosome in mouse spermatides.

Curator's Note: Interacts with the intraflagellar transport protein 88 (IFT88), involved in ciliogenesis and intraciliary transport. Required for ciliary localization of Polycystin-2, mediating the transport of Polycystin-2 from the ciliary base into the cilium (PMID: 27767179).
Localisation: Early and recycling endosomes, basal body (in the proximity interactome of several centriole distal appendage proteins)

Curator's Note: Positive regulator of the Hh signalling pathway, interacting with Smo and promoting Sufu/Gli3 dissociation and Gli3 ciliary traffic (PMID: 17660199, PMID: 23026747, PMID: 21356043, PMID: 22986504,PMID: 22981989). Mutated in Ellis-van Creveld syndrome (PMID: 21356043). EVC1 and EVC2 are mutually required for localizing to primary cilia and also for maintaining their normal protein levels (PMID: 23026747).

Also known as SEC6. Inhibition of ciliary shedding, blocks deciliation-associated down-regulation of claudin-2 and gp135 (PMID:19005211). Sec6/8 complex cooperates with cooperate with syntaxin 3 and SNAP-25, ceing a candidate effector for Rab8 at the rhodopsin transport carriers (RTC) docking site (PMID: 19454479)
Localisation: Primary cilia, domains in the vicinity of RTC fusion sites

Curator's Note: Also known as SEC10. Central and particularly important exocyst component required for exocyst formation and function. Regulation of primary ciliogenesis and cystogenesis through interactions with Par3 (PMID: 19297529, PMID: 30824539). Linker for other exocyst components, and interacts with polycystin-2, IFT20 and IFT88. Dysfunction may contribute to ciliopathies including autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease ADPKD (PMID: 21490950).
Localisation: Entire length of primary cillium, and tight junction.

Curator's Note: Also known as Sec15. Interacts with Rabin8 and is a downstream effector of Rab8. Rabin8-Rab8-Sec15 interaction is involved in the regulation of vesicular trafficking, tethering, and fusion for primary cilium formation. Disruption of function of Sec15 leads to a block of endosomal recycling and impaired ciliogenesis (PMID: 22433857, PMID: 23435566).

Description: enhancer of zeste 2 polycomb repressive complex 2 subunit(EZH2)
Curator's Note: Methyltransferase unit of PRC2. EZH2 suppresses genes functionally connected to the primary cilium, promoting loss of primay cilia; inhibition induces primary cilium formation in most melanoma cell. Loss of cilia

Description: family with sequence similarity 92 member A(FAM92A)
Curator's Note: Interact with Cby1 to promote ciliogenesis via regulation of membrane-remodeling processes, inducing the formation of membrane globule like structures, which contain Rab8 (PMID: 27528616). Mutated in nonsyndromic postaxial polydactyly. Role in limb development (PMID: 30395363).

Description: family with sequence similarity 92 member B(FAM92B)
Curator's Note: Cby1-interacting partner to promote ciliogenesis through regulation of membrane- remodeling processes, inducing the formation of membrane tubule like structures, which contain Rab8 (PMID: 27528616).

Description: family with sequence similarity 161 member A(FAM161A)
Curator's Note: Causative gene for retinitis pigmentosa (PMID: 20705278). Retinal ciliopathy protein that is part of connecting cillium complex. Interacts with CEP290, lebercin, OFD1 and SDCCAG8. These interactions suggest that FAM161A could be involved in protein transport and docking between the inner segments and outer plexiform layer (PMID: 22940612). Component of microtubule- organizing centers that associates with the intracellular microtubule network to increase the acetylation of α-tubulin. Involved in microtubule stabilization to maintain the microtubule tracks and/or in transport processes along cytoplasmic and ciliary microtubules (PMID: 24664697, PMID: 22791751).
Localisation: Connecting cillium, basal body, adjacent centriole, centrosome. Inner segments and outer plexiform layer

Description: family with sequence similarity 183 member B, pseudogene(FAM183BP)
Curator's Note: Required for ciliogenesis and motility of epidermal multiciliated cells and nephrostomes. Interaction partner of nucleoporin NUP93, which may function as scaffolding proteins at the ciliary base.

Transition fiber protein required for ciliogenesis and the ciliary import of assembled intraflagellar transport particles at the cilia base (PMID: 24231678). Functions in centriole duplication by recruiting HsSAS‐6 and promotes centrosome separation (PMID: 30318703).
Localisation: Distal appendages of mother centriole, proximal end of centrioles, transition fibers.

Curator's Note: Interacts with ICK to regular¿te ciliogenesis and control ciliary length (PMID: 30782830). FGFR3 signaling affects the elongation process of the primary cilia. Constitutively active FGFR3 perturbed cilia length, sorting and trafficking of intraflagellar transport 20 (PMID: 29040558). Mutations in FGFR3 lead to short primary cilia, and constitutive activation of FGFR3 signaling produces the skeletal disorders achondroplasia and thanatophoric dysplasia (PMID: 29360984).

Coordination of cytoskeletal dynamics during normal cilia assembly. Interacts with CEP170 to regulare cilia elongation and inhibition of cilia assembly. Overexpression of FHDC1 induces F-actin accumulation, microtubule stabilization, blocks cilia assembly and induces cilia resorption
Localisation: Cytoplasmic microtubules converging on the base of the cilia.

Curator's Note: Part of the mechanosensory machinery of primary cilia. Tumor suppressor associated with Birt-Hogg-Dubé (BHD) syndrome. Down-regulation of mTORC1 signaling pathway through primary cilia, it recruits and associates with LKB1 and recruits the kinase to primary cilia for activation of AMPK (PMID: 27072130). FLCN expression levels are critically important for correct timing of ciliogenesis and intracellular transport events involved in ciliogenesis (PMID: 23784378).
Localisation: Motile and non-motile cilia, centrosomes, mitotic spindle, cytoplasm, nucleus.

Curator's Note: Role in the normal processes of ciliogenesis and basal body positioning. Interacts with meckelin to regulate levels of Wnt signalling. Knockdown causes a failure in ciliogenesis and aberrant migration of the centriole pair to the apical cell surface suggestion FLNA is essential in mediating basal body migration and docking at the apical cell surface (PMID: 22121117, PMID: 28973524).
Localisation: Basal body, transition zone and apical cell surface.

Curator's Note: Regulation of integrity of the centriole distal end and membrane anchoring. Complex with OFD1 to initiate ciliogenesis and control cilia length (PMID: 26643951). Involved in cilia formation and regulating the interaction of PCM1 satellites with microtubules and motors (PMID: 20551181). Regulates the assembly and maintains the stability and dynamics of microtubules. It may inhibit tubulin assembly by sequestering soluble tubulin (PMID: 28694353).

Transcription factor that controls motile cilia formation (PMID: 19011630). Activates the transcription of numerous known ciliary genes and specifically regulates motile cilia biogenesis (PMID: 30881373). Regulation of programs promoting basal body docking and axoneme formation. Role of FOXJ1 in the differentiation of motile ciliated cells is modulated by the transcription factor Not homeobox (NOTO) and the regulatory factor X (RFX)- family (PMID: 23822649)

Description: fibronectin type III and SPRY domain containing 1(FSD1)
Curator's Note: Anchors microtubules asters to interphase centrosomes by directly binding microtubules to mother centriole, and controls transition zone assembly during ciliogenesis

Major structural protein of the fibrous sheath (FS) shown to bind to AKAP4, required for FS assembly. Regulaties PKA anchoring to AKAP4. Involved in the control of sperm flagellum elasticity and signaling pathways that regulate sperm motility. Mutations in FSIP2 are a recurrent cause of multiple morphological abnormalities of the sperm flagella.
Novel regulator of ciliogenesis in a non-cell autonomous manner due to its activity as a BMP4 inhibitor. BBS4 regulates the cellular trafficking of FSTL1.
Localisation: Cytoplasms (intracellular vesicles), secreted protein expected to be in the lumen of the Golgi and post-Golgi vesicles

Curator's Note: Candidate disease gene in heterotaxy. Modifies Notch to establish an essential balance between motile and immotile cilia at the left-right organiser, necessary to determine laterality.
Neuronal ciliary GPCR. Galanin receptor.
Neuronal ciliary GPCR. Galanin receptor.

Role in ciliary motility. Implicated in the Hh signaling pathway by binding to Smo and regulating its traficking into the cilium (PMID: 21659505). Mutations are associated with human disease as a cause of severe PCD phenotypes (PMID: 27472056).
Localisation: Axoneme of motile cilia, base of primary cilia, vesicles in cytoplasm.

Curator's Note: Hedgehog signaling pathway effector. GLI1 activation depends on cilia.

Hedgehog signaling pathway effector. Cilia or interflagellar transport proteins are required for GLI2 function and regulation (PMID: 21209912). Regulates autophagy- mediated Ofd1 removal to control primary cilia formation and length (PMID: 30463852).

Bifunctional transcriptional regulator, either as an activator and a repressor (PMID: 11741991). Repressor of Hh signaling. Loss of function causes nephronophthisis-like phenotype (PMID: 27181777). Involved in epithelial-to- mesenchymal transition, fibrosis and apoptosis. Together with BBS1, GLIS2 (also called NPHP7) is required for normal ciliary motility, responsible for body assymmetry (PMID: 24069149).

Also known as GEMC1. Regulator of multiciliated cells differentiation, interacting with E2F4/5‐DP1 and Multicilin. Candidate gene for human reduced generation of multiple motile cilia RGMC (PMID: 26933123). It transactivates the McIdas and FoxJ1 upstream regulatory sequences, markers of ciliogenesis (PMID: 26882546).
Subunit of transducin. Localises to photoreceptor outer segment. Requires RP2 for normal localisation

Required for ciliogenesis and control of ciliary length, through the lregulation of pericentrosomal location of the dynein-2 intermediate chain WDR34. Depletion results in cilia number and structure (fewer but longer cilia) (PMID: 28546340, PMID: 24046448).

Also known as TGR5. Linked to ERK signaling, which is activated in ciliated cholangiocytes but inhibited in nonciliated cholangiocytes. Involved in bile acid-induced proliferation of nonciliated cells. Its localisation allows cholangiocyte functional responses to bile acid signaling.
Localisation: Apical plasma, ciliary, and nuclear membrane

Curator's Note: Also known as SREB3. Neuronal ciliary GPCR which may play sensory or signalling roles in the ciliary vesicle or procilium during ciliogenesis
Localisation: Adjacent centriole and the basal body of the connecting cilium

Curator's Note: Neuronal ciliary GPCR
Localisation: Adjacent centriole and the basal body of the connecting cilium

Curator's Note: Regulation of Left-Right asymmetry through the Kupffer’s vesicle (KV) and mantains cilia length and structure in KV.
Regulation of D1 dopamine receptor (D1R) signaling to inhibit cAMP accumulation, whitout affecting B2AR- mediated response.

Also known as AGS3. Regulation fo Gβγ signaling pathway to recruits phospho(T94)Tctex-1 to the transition zone. Stabilises the GDP-bound form of Gαi wit IGF-1R to prevent its re- association with Gβγ and mantain it free.
Localisation: Base of the cilium, basal body.

Curator's Note: Phosphorylation of opsins, playing a key role in the shutdown of the rod and cone cascades (PMID: 25422369). Peripherally associated proteins anchored to the membrane by lipid modifications. It inactivates rhodopsin through phosphorylation (PMID: 25550383).

Involved in primary cilia elongation, microtubule assembly, stability and dynamics. Modulates CRMP- 2 ciliary localisation, and its ephosphorylated state is required for ciliary function (PMID: 23185275). Ciliary- maintenance signalling network, its disruption causes loss of cilia (PMID: 17450132). Phosphorylates Sufu and stabilises it against Shh signaling-induced degradation (PMID: 21317289).

HTT-HAP1-dynactin complex facilitates microtubule dependent vesicular transport. Regulates PCM1 trafficking and interacts with and huntingtin to control ciliogenesis. Depletion leads to dispersion of PCM1 from centrosomes and reduced ciliogenesis in cells. (PMID: 21985783).

Regulation of ciliary resorption in response to extracelullar stress and it is also a downstream AurA effector. Destabilises the microtubular axoneme through deacetylation of tubulin, which promotes ciliary disassembly (PMID: 17604723, PMID: 24026243). Mediates an autophagy- dependent mechanism called ciliophagy (PMID: 24200693)
Maintains the chondrocytes healthy under hypoxia (PMID: 31357086). Stabilised by USP8 through deubiquitination, which is essential for its ciliogenesis- promoting function (PMID: 24378640).

HNF1B deficiency is associated with ciliary anomalies in cholangiocytes and causes renal cysts. Regulates bile duct formation (PMID: 22706971). Control of the transcription of several genes expressed in tubular epithelial cells and transcriptional activation of Tg737/Polaris. HNF1β is not directly necessary for ciliogenesis, nevertheless, it may regulate the expression of genes that play a crucial role in cilium function (PMID:
oxysterol synthase HSD11β2 participates in the production of Smoothened-activating cilia-localised oxysterols and promotes Hedgehog pathway activity.

Description: heat shock protein 90 alpha family class A member 1
Curator's Note: Effector protein in the FOXJ1 regulatory network (PMID: 30881373). Hsp90α shows chaperone activity that might facilitate protein assembly and disassembly during ciliogenesis. Phosphorylated Hsp90α is likely to be a component of the distal appendages in the mother centriole (PMID: 25359884).

Description: heat shock protein family A (Hsp70) member 8(HSPA8)
Curator's Note: Also called HSC70. Function in the formation or stabilization of IFT-cargo complexes working with MRJ. It may bind directly to IFT88 or to one or more additional TPR containing proteins within the IFT particle, which in turn recruit MRJ bound cargo proteins (PMID: 19302411).
Localisation: Inner and outer segments, basal body

Curator's Note: Also known as 5-HT6. Regulates length, morphology and function of neuronal primary cilia through ARL13B, influences cilia and axon initial segment. Involved in cognition and Alzheimer’s disease development (PMID: 28931427). Enable chemosensory functions in ciliated neurons to sense 5- HT in the immediate milieu (PMID: 10432491).
Localisation: Ciliary shaft, ciliary membrane of neural cilia.

Curator's Note: Mutated in Huntington's Disease. Scaffolding protein required for vesicular transport via interactions with microtubules and motor protein cargo adaptors such as HAP1 and dynactin. Functional role in autophagy (PMID: 26160070). Essential for protein trafficking to the centrosome and normal ciliogenesis. Retrograde trafficking of PCM1 regulated by HTT and HAP1 to control ciliogenesis (PMID: 21985783).
Localisation: Centrosome, pericentriolar satellites, basal body. Tip of axoneme of photoreceptor cilium

Curator's Note: Required for intraflagellar transport trafficking and for centrioles to form cilia. Loss of HYLS-1 results in severe defects in axoneme assembly and transition zone organisation, due to impaired entry of IFT machinery to the cilia via DYF-19 (PMID: 28411189). Ciliogenesis mediation by regulating the formation of the ciliary gate; minor role in transition zone assembly. Required for distal centriole elongation and recruiting distal centriole proteins (PMID: 32509774). Essential for the apical targeting and/or anchoring of centrioles/basal body at the plasma membrane, contributin to basal body organisation (PMID: 19656802).
Localisation: Ciliary base, remanant in centriole. Outer centriole wall during centriole assembly.

Curator's Note: Component of IFT-A complex, mutated in skeletal ciliopathies with kidney disease (PMID: 23418020). Associates with IFT122 and IFT144 to a stable IFT-A core subcomplex; indispensable for dynein proteins retrograde transport into the cytoplasm and flagellar assembly. Required for development and maintenance of outer segments, ciliary/flagellar assembly and signal transduction (PMID: 29236364, PMID: 24619649).

Component of IFT complex B. Involved in the switching between the anterograde and retrograde transport (PMID: 29659833). Essential for ciliary growth and maintenance, and morphogenesis of the cerebral cortex. Mutation cause alterations in multiple intracellular signaling pathways (PMID: 31850339, PMID: 18930042). Mutations are associated with severe skeleto-renal disorders with retinal involvement (PMID: 25168386).

Also known as RABL5, component of IFT complex B. Controls the cellular levels of both IFT‐A and IFT‐B proteins and to regulate availability of particles participating in IFT (PMID: 30940671). Recruitment of BBSome to the basal body through BBS3 and regulation of BBSome entry into the cilia (PMID: 31953262).
Localisation: Basal body, cilium, cell body, IFT

Curator's Note: Also known as RABL4, component of IFT complex B. Forms a complex with IFT25 and associates with IFT-B inside cilia, interacts with and stabilises the nucleotide-free form of ARL6 to promote the exit of BBSome out of cilia. Mutated in Bardet-Biedl syndrome (PMID: 25443296). Required for BBSome trafficking essential for hedgehog signaling. IFT25/IFT27 complex plays a role in transporting Gli2 to the ciliary tip (PMID: 25446516). Role in the cargo loading of the retrograde transport machinery (PMID: 24843028).

Component of IFT complex B, required for ciliogenesis and controls cilia number and length (PMID: 25722189). Plas a role in the transport of IFT proteins between the cytoplasm and cilia (PMID: 29915351). IFT46 is crucial for transport of ODA16 into the flagellum; it interacts with IFT52 to assembly a subcomplex which is a prerequisite for the assembly of IFT-B1 (PMID: 28701346).

Component of IFT complex B. Essential for anterograde complex integrity, biosynthesis and maintenance of cilia. Regulation of ciliogenesis and cilia length; it also plays a role as a docking site for complex B proteins attaching to the transition fibres of the basal bodies and is required for localization of the IFT-B complex proteins (PMID: 27466190). Recruits and interacts with IFT46 to assembly a subcomplex which is a prerequisite for the assembly of IFT-B1, it is also required to localise IFT46 to the basal body (PMID: 28302912).

Component of IFT complex B. Interacts with IFT81 to stabilise IFT-B complex. This interaction is required for binding and transport of tubulin to regulate cilium length, required for ciliogenesis (PMID: 23990561). Essential for normal mouse spermatogenesis and sperm flagella formation by transporting cargo proteins and modulating axoneme and microtubule assembly (PMID: 31004481).

Component of IFT complex B. Role in cilia formation and osteogenesis through regulating Hedgehog/Gli signal pathways. Silencing IFT80 led to either shortening or loss of cilia and the decrease of cilia marker protein Arl13b expression. Mutations cause Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy (JATD) and short rib polydactyly type III (SRPIII) (PMID: 22771375). Required for IFT mediated recruitment and transport of ciliary cargo, as well as for initiation of the ciliary axoneme (PMID: 29658880).

Component of IFT complex B. Required for ciliary and flagellar assembly and may play a role in the attachment of the IFT particle to its cargo or to the anterograde IFT motor FLA10-kinesin-II (PMID: 11062270).

IGF-1 signals are predominantly transduced through IGF-1 receptor (IGF- 1R) on the cilia. Promotes cell cycle entry. Mediation of ciliary resorption through activation of IGF-1R (PMID: 23954591). IGF1 mediated signaling regulates ciliated cell differentiation (PMID: 28050756).

Activation of an AGS3- regulated Gβγ signaling pathway that subsequently recruits phospho(T94)Tctex-1 to the transition zone, leading to cilia resorption (PMID: 23954591). IGF1R mediated plays a role in regulating ciliated cell differentiation (PMID: 28050756).
Localisation: Cell surface, primary cillium, ciliary membrane.

Curator's Note: Regulator of transition zone function. INPP5E may regulate Hedgehog signaling via modulating the PI(4,5)P2- dependent recruitment of GPR161 to cilia. It is essential for maximal SMO accumulation at cilia after the Hh pathway (PMID: 27998989). Controls ciliary growth factor, PI3K signaling and stability (PMID: 19668215). Mutations cause Joubert Syndrome and promotes premature destabilization of cilia (PMID: 19668216).
Localisation: Axoneme, adjacent to the base of the cilium

Curator's Note: Governs apical actin assembly and thus controls the orientation, but not assembly, of ciliary microtubules (PMID: 16493421, PMID: 27158779). Cilia and planar polarity effector, essential for IFT-A complex assembly during ciliogenesis, forming a molecular module with Fuzzy (FUZ) and WDPCP. INTU functions upstream of Gli2 activation and is required for Smo-mediated Hh pathway activation (PMID: 28459465).

Also known as NPHP5. Required for extension of an axoneme after docking of the basal body to the cell membrane. Absence leads to mislocalization of BBS2, BBS5 and destroys BBSome integrity (PMID: 27328943). Interacts with CEP290 and is required for early cilia assembly, migration and/or anchoring of centrosomes to the cell cortex (PMID: 23446637). NPHP5-binding to the BBSome is crucial for BBSome integrity and ciliary trafficking (PMID: 25552655).
Localisation: Basal Body, distal region of centriolles, proximal outer segments

Curator's Note: Form a complex with EFCAB7. It anchors the EVC- EVC2 complex to positively regulate the Hh pathway (PMID: 24582806)
Required for cilogenesis and spermiogenesis in mammals through a dynamic interaction with calmodulin in different intracellular calcium levels (PMID: 24849454).

Ubiquitin ligase targeting β- catenin for proteasomal degradation. Component of the NPHP protein complex, interacting with NPHP4 which facilitates JADE-1 nuclear traslocation, leading to decreased canonical Wnt signaling (PMID: 22654112, PMID: 25100726).
Localisation: Transition zone, basal body, nucleus, cytosol.

Curator's Note: Regulator of multiciliated cell differentiation. It may function upstream of Foxj1 expression (PMID: 29661797).

Required for ciliogenesis and proper differentiation of radial glia to functional ependymal cells. Mutations cause congenital hydrocephalus and loss of JHY results in the lack of the ciliary microtubule central pair (PMID: 29211732).

Required for dynamic regulation of microtubules during axoneme formation and maintenance; it may have the ability to remodel microtubules at different cellular locations. Role during the regulation of Wnt/planar cell polarity (PCP)-dependent processes. Required for ciliogenesis, organogenesis and brain size control (PMID: 30096282). Interacts with Nubp1 and Nubp2 AAA proteins, which act as negative regulators of ciliogenesis (PMID: 26153462).
Localisation: Basal body and ciliary axoneme in multiciliated cells, centriolles of non- ciliated cells and mitotic spindles.

Description: potassium voltage-gated channel modifier subfamily F member 1(KCNF1)
Curator's Note: Ion channel gene that exhibits a significant negative effect on ciliogenesis but not on cell number. Potential new candidate in human ciliopathies (PMID: 26546361).
Localisation: Membrane subdomains at the base of primary cilia.

Description: potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily H member 1(KCNH1)
Curator's Note: Also known as Kv10.1. Promotes ciliary disassembly and cell progression through localised changes of membrane potential at the ciliary base (PMID: 28370099). Interacts with proteins involved in ciliary regulation, such as Rabaptin 5, cortactin, and HIF (PMID: 27113750).

Description: potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily J member 13(KCNJ13)
Curator's Note: Mutations are associated with the human retinal dystrophies LCA and Snowflake Vitreoretinal Degeneration (PMID: 30009826).

Description: potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily Q member 1(KCNQ1)
Curator's Note: Ion channel gene that exhibits a significant negative effect on ciliogenesis but not on cell number. Genetic variants are known to cause Long QT syndrome. KCNQ1 could be implicated in renal ciliopathies (PMID: 26546361).
Localisation: Membrane subdomains at the base of primary cilia.

Curator's Note: Component of cullin-3– RBX1–KCTD10 complex mediating CEP97 degradation and removal from the mother centriole, as well as removal of CP110 from the mother centriole to promote primary cilium formation. Binding partner of B9D1, mutations of which cause ciliopathies (PMID: 30404837).

Negative regulator of ciliogenesis required for the controlled recruitment of IFT proteins into cilia through the modulation of actin dynamics. It binds to the actin cytoskeleton, creating a responsive actin gate involving ARP2/3 activity and regulating IFT within cilia and periciliary compartments. In the absence of KDM3A, access to cilia is unrestricted, so the assembly and growth of primary cilia is enhanced (PMID: 28246120).
Mutations are associated with Retinitis Pigmentosa (PMID: 30120214).
Localisation: Connecting cilium of the photoreceptor cells, synapses of the mouse retina

Curator's Note: Binds to microtubules and stabilise microtubule networks when overexpressed; it interacts with intraflagellar transport components and katanins associated with microtubules severing.
