Form a complex that regulates microtubule dynamics as well as ciliary functions. Negative regulator of ciliary length. Mutated in Joubert syndrome (PMID: 27245168, PMID:

Required for ciliogenesis and sonic hedgehog/SHH signaling. Role in primary cilia formation and microtubule organisation (PMID: 19144723). Component of a CP110-containing protein complex required for centrosome and cilia function, Required for the centrosomal recruitment of RAB8A and for the targeting of centriole satellite proteins to centrosomes such as of PCM1. May play a role in early ciliogenesis in the disappearance of centriolar satellites that preceeds ciliary vesicle formation. Essential for centrosomal migration prior to ciliogenesis (PMID: 24421332). Mutated in Joubert syndrome (PMID: 26096313) and in skeletal ciliopathies (PMID: 31816441; PMID: 32080096)
Localisation: Centrosome, distal end of centrioles, basal body

Curator's Note: Mutated cause impaired ciliogenesis and result in Joubert Syndrome. Regulates centriole duplication positively by recruiting CDK2 to the centrosome, as well as WDR62 to the pericentriolar complex, which in turn recruits CEP63; interacts with CEP63, and regulate CEP63 level at the centrosome(PMID: 28220259, PMID: 24613305). Also cause skeletal ciliopathies (PMID: 31816441; PMID: 29138412).

Regulator of chromosome segregation, cytokinesis and midbody formation. Regulator of cilia formation, basal body biogenesis and Hedgehog (HH) signaling. Depletion of KIF14 specifically leads to defects in ciliogenesis and basal body biogenesis (PMID: 32348467). Mutations in humans and zebrafish cause ciliopathy-like kidney and microcephaly phenotypes (PMID: 30388224; PMID: 24128419)
Localisation: Primary cillium axoneme, spindle, nucleus, cytoplasm

Curator's Note: Interacts with importin-β2 and Rab23 (PMID: 26136363). Motor protein that may be needed to position the ciliary localization signal CLS- containing protein at the ciliary base (PMID: 20526328). Interacts with the IFT46–IFT56 dimer in the IFT- B complex (PMID: 28077622). Required for photoreceptor OS formation and protein targeting; implicated in ciliary membrane protein trafficking (PMID: 18304522).
Localisation: Basal body, axoneme, distal tip of the primary cilium, cytoplasm.

Curator's Note: Promotes the primary cilium disassembly through its microtubule-depolymerising activity at the mother centriole, coupled with cell proliferation and blocking inappropriate ciliogenesis during the cycling phase. Controls the cytoplasmic tubulin concentration to regulate primary cilia disassembly (PMID: 25660017). Mutations cause primary microcephaly. Recruited by CEP170 (PMID: 31197141).
Localisation: Basal body, subdistal appendages of the mother centrioles

Curator's Note: Physiological substrate of Nek2. It prevents the outgrowth of cilia in proliferating cells. Ensure the disassembly of a ciliary axoneme in the later stages of the cell cycle (PMID: 26290419). Interacts with CP110 and Cep97. Regulates ciliogenesis by dynamically controlling microtubule polymerisation (PMID: 21620453). Controls the formation of primary cilia by restricting the nucleation of cilia at centrioles, it regulates CP110 localisation at mother centrioles (PMID: 21663786).
Localisation: Centrioles, it preferentially localises to the distal end of mother centriole

Curator's Note: Required for cilia assembly, function and organisation of subdistal appendiges of centrioles. Recruits p150Glued to the subdistal appendages of mother centrioles, critical for centrosomes to function as microtubule-organising centres and to recruit other subdistal appendage components such as Ninein and Cep170. Loss of Kif3a abrogates microtubule anchoring and ciliary basal foot formation (PMID: 23386061).

Essential for ciliogenesis and the left–right asymmetry through intraciliary transportation of materials for ciliogenesis of motile cilia that produces the nodal flow (PMID: 9865700). Its phosphorylation inhibits IFT entry and flagellar lengthening restricting flagellar assembly (PMID: 30057303).

Inhibitory role on cilia extension. Interacts with CCDC28B to regulate cilia length and the sub-cellular distribution of CCDC28B (PMID: 29445114). Required for intraflagellar transport and the formation of primary cilia (PMID: 31636894).
Localisation: Pericentriolar region at the basal body

Curator's Note: Mediator of ciliogenesis and normal cilia beating in ependmal cells in vertebrates. Mutations are reported to be associated with neurological abnormalities in humans (PMID: 30475797).
Localisation: Axoneme and basal body of motile cilia

Curator's Note: Negative regulator of Hedgehog signalling at cilia in mammals by controlling the activity of Gli and Sufu. Controls the localization of Hh signaling complexes through its ability to regulate the dynamics of microtubule plus- ends. It inhibits microtubule growth to regulate the length of axonemal microtubules at the ciliary tip and control cilia structure (PMID: 24981634, PMID: 24952464, PMID: 19592253). A conserved non- motile kinesin, Kif7 defines a "cilium-tip compartment" by localizing to the distal ends of

Required for ciliary membrane protein transport and serum starvation–induced ciliogenesis. Role in the Golgi transport of membrane proteins from the Golgi complex to the primary cilium and in the recruitment of ciliogenesis regulators and maintenance. Required for TTBK2 recruitment and CP110 removal from the distal end of the mother centriole to iniciate cilium assembly (PMID: 29042452).
Ciliary receptor which plays a role in reproductive function. Cilia are required for proper Kiss1r-mediated signaling on GnRH neurons

Interacts with PLK1 in order to protect the centrosome from collapsing during spindle formation in mitosis. KIZ might have a critical role in this trafficking process. Mutations lead to autosomal- recessive Rod-Cone Dystrophy (PMID: 24680887).

Essential for the trafficking of proteins and vesicles to the photoreceptor outer segment. Mutations cause retinal degeneration, including cone dystrophy and autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa (PMID: 29673930, PMID: 21606596, PMID: 18826961). Interacts with a nearly complete IFT complex B particle, as well as with some IFT complex A proteins (PMID: 21606596).
Localisation: Basal Body, centrosome, primary Cilium, microtubule network.

Curator's Note: Also known as EPLIN. Modulates actin stability to restrict primary cilia formation. Knockdown increases the levels of MyosinVa at the centrosome and primary cilia formation (PMID: 32496561)

Actin remodelling factor. Role in the negative regulation of ciliogenesis by upregulating the expression of YAP/TAZ target genes. Together with TESK1, LIMK2 plays a role in suppressing the directional trafficking of ciliary vesicles to the ciliary base (PMID: 25849865).

Radial spoke protein with function in ciliary motility and motile cilia formation. Mutations in Lrrc23 result in ciliary motility defects specifically in the cilia of the otic vesicle (PMID: 29475374).

Mutated in Joubert syndrome. Localized along the ciliary shaft in controls but only at ciliary base in LRRC34-/- patient cells, which displayed reduced ciliogenesis potential and muted response of SHH signaling to SAG compared with controls (PMID: 32055034)

Recruits the keratin-binding protein FBF1. Promotes cilia biogenesis in CP110- uncapped centrioles by organising centriolar satellites. It is required for centrosome cohesion at the proximal end of centrioles. Establishes the transition zone, recruitment of Rab8 and satellites to centrosomes, and promotes the docking of Rab8 GTPase-positive vesicles to the mother centriole (PMID: 30131441).

Plays a role in cytoplasmic preassembly of dynein arms, essential for proper axonemal assembly (PMID: 23122589). Involved in the transport of the preassembled outer dynein arm complex to the axoneme and in transcriptional regulation of some dynein proteins (PMID: 27353389 PMID: 23527195). Mutations lead to primary ciliary dyskinesia with laterality defects (PMID: 23527195)
Localisation: Cilia, cytoplasm, proximal to basal body

Curator's Note: Phosphorylates Rab8A, Rab10 and Rab12, mutations interferer with primary cilia formation by generating pRab10 that binds endogenous RILPL1 and blocks cilia formation. Regulates intracellular vesicular traffic during ciliogenesis (PMID: 30398148, PMID: 29125462).
Localisation: Lysosome, ER, endosome, Golgi, mitochondiral outer membrane

Curator's Note: Localizes to both actin filaments and the centrosome/basal body. Is an actin-stabilizing protein that regulates actin dynamics, at least in part, by mobilizing ARP2 to the centrosomes. Interacts with known ciliogenesis and cilia-length regulators. Depleting LUZP1 or its interacting protein, EPLIN, increases the levels of MyosinVa at the centrosome and primary cilia formation

Interacts with a BBS protein complex known as the BBSome to negatively regulate ciliary trafficking of this complex inhibiting BBSome ciliary entry. It also regulates ciliary trafficking of hedgehog signal transducer, Smoothened (PMID: 22072986). Coordinates the interactions between the BBSome and the IFT particle to regulate the removal of Ptch1 and Smo from cilia (PMID: 25446516). Depletion leads to a Bardet-Biedl syndrome phenotype (PMID: 22510444).

Role in coordination of actin and microtubules; critical in ciliogenesis, maintenance and regulation of apicobasal polarity. Potential interacting partner with basal body protein Mkks and TALPID3. It may be required for cilia- targeted vesicle exchange at this actin/microtubule interface. Loss of Macf1 abolished docking of the basal body and subsequent extension of the ciliary axoneme (PMID: 27783952).
Localisation: Distal end of microtubules, Cytoskeleton, cytoplasm, around the base of the connecting cilium.

Curator's Note: Involved in the regulation of photoreceptor connecting cilium length. Mutations cause autosomal dominant Retinitis Pigmentosa (PMID: 22110072). Essential for the regulation of ciliary length, preventing excessive elongation of the cilia and is required for the long-term survival of photoreceptors (PMID: 21148103). Forms a complex with DYF-5 to regulate cilia morphology ikely via modulation of microtubule stability (PMID: 30955935).
Localisation: Connecting cilia and outer segment axonemes

Curator's Note: MAL overexpression is associated with shortened or absent cilia, abnormal cilium and cyst development. MAL may facilitate the organisation of apical cargo into microdomains to facilitate their targeting and trafficking (PMID: 22895261). Involved in the proper condensation of membranes at the ciliary base, required for efficient primary cilium extension (PMID: 25967552).
Localisation: Punctuated distribution in the cillium, apical plasma membrane, ciliary base.

Description: microtubule associated protein RP/EB family member 1(MAPRE1)
Curator's Note: Also known as EB1. Required for assembly of primary cilia, interacting with proteins implicated in microtubule minus-end anchoring at the centrosome to facilitate vesicular trafficking to the cilia base (PMID: 21768326, PMID: 17600711).
Localisation: Proximal region of the basal body, centrosome: close to subdistal appendages of the mother centriole. Flagellar tip.

Curator's Note: ERK2. Downstream of TGFBR1 and 2, which phosphorylate ERK1/2 at base of cilium upon TGFB stimulation

Regulates motile and primary cilia formation, and the localisation of ciliary proteins involved in cilium structure, signaling and trasport like BBS7 and ARL-13 (PMID: 29021280). Required for basal body migration and apical actin organisation in multiciliated cells, it is also important for left-right axis specification. Phosphorylates CapZIP, in cooperation with Dishevelled (PMID: 25823377).

Also known as SIN1. Component of the mTOR complex 2. Interacts with CCDC28B to regulate cilia length and inhibits MEKK2, which activates different MAPKs that have been implicated in the regulation of IFT and ciliogenesis (PMID: 23727834, PMID: 26263164).
E3 ubiquitin ligase, works with USP9X to ubiquitinate NPHP5 and regulate ciliogenesis (PMID: 28498859).

Required for initiation of axoneme extension during early ciliogenesis, after the docking of Rab8a-positive vesicles to the mother centriole. Regulates ODF2 localisation to the centriole (PMID: 23400999).

Description: multiciliate differentiation and DNA synthesis associated cell cycle protein(MCIDAS)
Curator's Note: Promotes multiciliated cell formation during multiciliate cell differentiation. Mutations lead to severe axonemal defects, lack of ciliary motility- related proteins (PMID: 25048963). Promotes the transcriptional changes required for motile ciliogenesis and centriole assembly; it induces motile cilia outgrowth via FoxJ1, centriole assembly and basal body formation. Regulates the genes required for multiciliated cells differentiation (PMID: 22231168, PMID: 26933123).
Involved in the primary cilia shortening through a unique signal from the ciliary membrane (PMID: 32240710). Candidate ciliary GPCR (PMID: 18256283).

Function in transcriptional regulation/inhibition of genes involved in ciliogenesis and centrosome duplication. Helps to control left-right asymmetry development in zebrafish, facilitates formation and hence proper function of motile and primary cilia. Likely controls cilia length . Loss of MCM2 promotes transcription

Required for dynein- dependent cargo transport to the centrosome. Interacts with the dynein intermediate chain DYNC1I1, and plays an essential role in both the establishment of centriolar satellites and the initiation of primary cilium assembly. MCRS1 also mediates centriolar recruitment of TTBK2 (PMID: 27263857).

Upregulated during ciliogenesis (PMID: 23300604). Microtubule- binding protein. Negative regulator of centriole duplication through microtubule binding. Overexpression of MDM1 suppresses centriole duplication and results in stabilization of microtubules (PMID: 26337392). It might interact with members of the Hedgehog signaling pathway, as this pathway is tightly linked with cilia (PMID: 27658201)
Localisation: Mid-proximal region of centriole, in the lumen of the centriole, cillium

Curator's Note: Interacts with and ubiquitylates AZI1 and PCM1, regulates the composition and function of centriolar satellites and suppresses primary ciliogenesis (PMID: 24121310). MIB1 destabilizes Talpid3 through poly- ubiquitylation and suppresses cilium assembly (PMID: 27146717). It redistributes to centrioles in response to

Regulates the supply of molecular components to the apical membranes of photoreceptors in order to control the maintenance of outer segments, formation of inner segments, connecting cilia, and outer segments in a developing retina culture in vitro (PMID: 25002228).

Regulates the supply of molecular components to the apical membranes of photoreceptors in order to control the maintenance of outer segments, formation of inner segments, connecting cilia, and outer segments in a developing retina culture in vitro (PMID: 25002228). Depletion results in the upregulation of Rnf217 and misregulation of cilia-related genes (PMID: 32176259).

Required for the multiciliogenesis of multiciliated cells in the kidney and olfactory placode. It plays essential roles in the formation and organisation of cilia bundles. Serves as a guardian to maintain optimal levels of cmyb (PMID: 23698347). Essential for normal brain development, motile ciliogenesis, and spermatogenesis (PMID: 24982181).

Also known as BBS6. Associated with Bardet-Biedl and McKusick-Kaufman syndromes. Chaperonin-like BBS protein necessary for BBSome assembly in associationg with BBS10 and BBS12, and required for the stability of BBS2 and BBS7 (PMID: 20080638). Interacts with CEP290 in the ciliary transition zone to mediate ciliogenesis, maintenance of cilia integrity and function (PMID: 22446187).

Required for ciliogenesis of motile and non-motile cilia and post-migration of the centriole to the plasma membrane. Plays an essential role in modulating signaling in the non-canonical Wnt signaling pathway (PMID: 21045211). Modulates centrosome duplication to regular cilia length and number; mutants exhibite fewer and shorter cilia (PMID: 21045211, PMID: 19515853). Interacts with BBS4 to mediate trafficking of subset of membrane proteins to the primary cilium. Role in the structure of the cilia tip compartment (PMID: 28291807). Regulates ciliary INPP5E content (PMID: 26490104).
Localisation: Mother centriole, basal body, transition zone

Curator's Note: Known to cause heterotaxy and primary ciliary dyskinesia (PMID: 30622330). Specialised role in the generation of left-right asymmetry (PMID: 26437028).

Role in outer dynein arm (ODA) docking in the distal axonemes, stabilising structures in the motile cilium that helps the attachment of motor proteins to the microtubules to ensure a correct beating of the cilia; interacts with the ODA docking complex component CCDC114 and DNAH5. Deficiency cases laterality defects (PMID: 30148830). Essential for the assembly of sperm flagella (PMID: 22396656).

Negative regulattion of cilium length through the inhibition of the mTORC1 pathway and suppressing the synthesis of ciliary tubulin. It is part of, or transported by the IFT machinery (PMID: 25243405).

Forms a ring-like structure and regulates ciliogenesis by modulating CP110-CEP97 complex recruitment and localization at the mother centriole, by directly binding CEP97, which blocks cilia assembly in cycling cells able to form cilia. degradation of MPP9 facilitates the removal of the CP110-CEP97 complex from basal bodies and promotes cilia formation (PMID: 30375385).

Mutations in MTOR Disrupt Neuronal Ciliogenesis and decreases cilia length, via induction of aberrant accumulation of OFD1 at centriolar satellites (PMID: 29937275). Downregulated by cilium bending, which in turn regulates cell size (PMID: 21145495). Inhibition of mTOR induces primary cilia formation; mTOR inhibition leads to the activation of autophagy, which suppresses the proteasome and prevents the degradation of ciliary proteins resulting in ciliogenesis (PMID: 32213867, PMID: 29180513, PMID: 25906314). Involved in the elongation and maintenance of cilium size by promoting the biosynthesis of proteins and lipids required for cilium elongation and maintenance (PMID: 29180513).
Localisation: Mitochondiron outer membrane, lysosome, ER, Golgi, cytoplasm

Curator's Note: Regulators of the actin cytoskeleton. Required for centriole migration to the apical plasma membrane during the biogenesis of primary cilia. Regulates centrosomal recruitment of IFT88 required for ciliary tip structure (PMID: 25881509). Required for pericentrosomal recruitment of Cep290, PCM- 1 and Rab11-positive recycling endosomes. It binds and antagonises Myh9 to increase actin dynamics and facilitate the assembly of the pericentrosomal preciliary complex that supplies materials for cilium growth and initiates ciliogenesis (PMID: 25494100).
Essential for the graded elongation of stereocilia during their functional maturation and staircase formation (PMID: 14610277).
Localisation: Ciliary Tip of Stereocilia under the apical plasma membrane

Curator's Note: Knockout results in reduction in ciliation, suggesting MYO5A is required for ciliogenesis. It might link microtubule cargo from Golgi or cilium (PMID: 28710093). It mediates the transportation of preciliary vesicles to the mother centriole, depletion inhibits the attachment of preciliary vesicles to the distal appendages of the mother centriole and decreases cilia assembly (PMID: 29335527). Interacts with the cilia- centrosomal protein RPGRIP1L (PMID: 28266547).
Localisation: Centrosome. Preciliary vesicle, ciliary vesicle and ciliary sheath

Curator's Note: Responsible for Usher syndrome type 1B (PMID:7870171). requiredfor normal hair cell development, as well as for thefunction of the mature hair cells (PMID: 9678669). It might be required for the transport of newly synthesized outer segment proteins to the site of disk membrane assembly (PMID: 9227854). Myosin VIIa participates in the transport of opsin through the connecting cilium (PMID: 10414956).
Localisation: Connecting cilium, photoreceptor axoneme, periphery of the transition zone

Description: neural precursor cell expressed, developmentally down- regulated 9(NEDD9)
Curator's Note: Transducer of integrin attachment, migration, and anti-apoptotic signals at focal adhesions. Promotes activation and stabilisation of AurA, which phosphorylates ciliary HDAC6 to induce disassembly of the primary cilium. (PMID: 17604723).

Role in centrosome integrity, affecting both ciliogenesis and centrosome stability; it may suppress cilia by phosphorylating VHL. NEK1 overexpression leads to cilia resorption in cultured cells. Mutations lead to defective cilia (PMID: 23255108). NEK1 binds to the microtubule‐ dependent motor protein, Kif3A, probably influencing microtubule‐dependent processes, including stabilization of axonemal microtubules (PMID: 18387364). Compites with CP110 for binding to the Cep104 ZNF domain. Mutations cause ciliopathies (PMID: 28017521),
Localisation: Basal body, pericentriolar satellite region of the centrosome

Curator's Note: Phosphorylates the centrosomal linker proteins C- Nap1, Cep68 and Rootletin to promote centriole separation, and is involved in the development of left-right asymmetry by regulating balancing ciliogenesis and resorption (PMID: 26493400). Phosphorylates Kif24, a depolymerising kinesin (PMID: 26290419). Influences centrosome-anchored microtubules organisation and promotes cilium disassembly at the onset of mitosis (PMID: 22613497). NEK2 removes distal appendage components from the mother centriole, preventing cilia maintenance during mitosis (PMID: 32211891).
Localisation: Proximal end of centroles, distal end of mother centriole, basal body.

Curator's Note: Interacts with RPGRIP1 and RPGRIP1L to regulate cilium integrity and/or assembly. It associates with ciliary rootlets to regulate cilia stability

Mutations cause nephronophthisis (NPHP9); it can be transported into cilia by Inv (PMID: 20169535). Controls or modulates the ciliary localization of PC1 and PC2, as well as ciliary length (PMID: 18235101). It is speculated that Nek8 activity may be required to initiate ciliogenesis, and degradation may be required to prevent it (PMID: 22106379). Component of the PC2 channel complex required to mediate nodal calcium flux, indispensable for the establishment of left-right asymmetry (PMID: 23274954).
Localisation: Centrosomes, proximal segment of cilia (Inv compartiments), cytoplasm, nucleus.

Curator's Note: Also called NRF2. Primary Cilium-Autophagy-Nrf2 (PAN) Axis Activation Commits Human Embryonic Stem Cells to a Neuroectoderm Fate (PMID: 27020754). Negative regulator of primary ciliogenesis (via p62) and the Hh signaling pathway (through PTCH1), which blocks ciliary traslocation of BBS4 and SMO (PMID: 32053600). Contradictory paper says that it promotes ciliogenesis (PMID: 31554934)

Likely to provide signals to drive granule cell progenitor proliferation (PMID: 22995307). It may be involved in neurogenesis and memory- encoding functions in dentate gyral granule cells (PMID: 20875398).

Also called NLP. It is involved in microtubule nucleation, anchoring and outgrowth (PMID: 18826961). NLP interacts with ciliopathy- associated proteins lebercilin, USH2A and CC2D2A. Interacts with DZANK1 in vesicle transport towards the photoreceptor outer segments and its development/maintenance, in photoreceptor cells (PMID: 26485514).

Facilitates DNA-repair mechanisms. Binds to several NPHPs, including NEK8, CEP164, and ankyrin repeat and sterile α motif domain- containing 6 (ANKS6). Required for determining left- right assymetry and ciliogenesis. Potential nephronophthisis disease gene (PMID: 30111592 ).
Hydrocephalus and infertility due to dysfunctional motile cilia in KO mouse (PMID: 21746835). Role in ciliary beating (PMID: 24424412). Mutations cause of human PCD (PMID: 32185794).

Also called TXNDC3, Candidate gene for PCD. Encodes a thioredoxine- nucleoside diphosphate kinase expressed in testis and respiratory epithelial cells. It is shown to have binding properties to microtubules (PMID: 17360648). Human ortholog of the sea urchin IC1 gene that encodes a component of sperm outer dynein arms (PMID: 19410201).
It is glycosylated by GALNT11 to establish an essential balance between motile and immotile cilia at the left-right organiser, controlling laterality (PMID: 24226769).
Involved in centrosome and cilia function. Causative gene in the majority of familial cases of nephronophthisis and recently associated with Joubert syndrome (PMID: 15138899, PMID: 22982934).

Mutations cause nephronophthisis type 3 (PMID: 22328406). Interaction with Inversin is essential for NPHP3 localisation (PMID: 20169535). Cooperates with Inversin and promotes ANKS6 phosphorylation by NEK8 in renal cilia. It may be involved in the regulation of noncanonical Wnt-pathway (PMID: 29395339).

Involved in familial juvenile nephronophthisis and retinitis pigmentosa. Component of the transition zone barrier that controls the movement of proteins between the flagellar and cytoplasmic compartments. Potentially interacts with MKS/B9 proteins to prevent ciliary membrane proteins from diffusing out of the cilium (PMID: 25150219). Probably involved in actin and microtubule organisation in cell–cell and cell–matrix adhesion signaling (PMID:
Encodes a G protein-coupled receptors involved in energy homeostasis, and could be a major driver of hyperphagia- induced obesity in BBS (PMID: 24316073).
Encodes a G protein-coupled receptors involved in energy homeostasis (PMID: 24316073).

Description: nuclear receptor subfamily 1 group H member 4(NR1H4)
Curator's Note: Regulates autophagy by controlling transcription of genes involved in autophagic pathways. It negatively regulares ciliogenesis by inhibiting autophagy (PMID: 29771182)..
Also called SDOS. Controls cilium biogenesis by regulating the translation of cilia mRNAs involved in ciliogenesis. Controls synthesis of constituent proteins of the primary cilium.
Localisation: Nucleus and cytoplasm (endoplasmic reticulum, associated translating ribosomes)

Curator's Note: Potential role in regulation of protein trafficking and polarised delivery of Cng channels to photoreceptor cilia, through recycling endosomes for delivery to OS plasma membrane (PMID: 25319694 ).
Localisation: Cytoplasm, inner segment of photoreceptor cilia.

Curator's Note: Encodes a protein of the inner ring of the nuclear pore complex. Implicated as causes of steroid resistant nephrotic syndrome. When knocked down in Xenopus, Nup205 depletion results in loss of cilia and abnormal cardiac morphology, and mispositioning of intracellular ciliary structures such as basal bodies and rootlets (PMID: 33065118). Downregulated in NEK3-/- patients who are predisposed to cilia-related abnormal cardiac left-right patterning
Inner ring nucleoporin, component of ciliary pore complex that regulares protein transport into cilia (PMID: 22388888)
Outer ring nucleoporin, component of ciliary pore complex that regulares protein transport into cilia (PMID: 22388888)

Central chanel nucleoporin, component of ciliary pore complex that regulares protein transport into cilia (PMID: 22388888). Involved in active transport of cytosolic proteins into both ciliary and nuclear compartments (PMID: 25264252).

Interact with Nek2 to regulate cilium integrity, as removal of Nup98 from the ciliary nucleoporin complex is mandatory for ciliary resorption (PMID: 26493400). Component of a diffusion barrier that limits diffusion of molecules >70kDa between cytoplasm and ciliary matrix.Knockdown of NUB98 stops cilium elongations, suggesting it is required for cilia length regulation (PMID: 29731308).

Interacts with GTPases and is involved in intracellular trafficking and cilia maintenance; mutation are associated with Lowe syndrome (PMID: 22543976). Required for cilia assembly by contributing to Rab8/IPIP27 dependent protein trafficking to the primary cilia (PMID: 22228094) and modulation of cilia length (PMID: 22680056). Required for primary cilia to respond to pressure stimulation through its interaction with vanilloid 4 (PMID: 25143588).
Localisation: Trans-Golgi network, basal body, transition zone and axoneme.

Description: OFD1, centriole and centriolar satellite protein(OFD1)
Curator's Note: Associated with oral-facial- digital type I syndrome. Absence of the Ofd1 protein leads to basal body dysfunction, which in turn prevents the assembly of the primary cilium, and causes failure of left-right axis specification (PMID: 16311594). It associates with the distal ends of centriolar microtubules to build distal appendages, recruit Ift88, and stabilise centriole length and regulate ciliogenesis (PMID: 20230748). Its presence at the centriolar satellite suppresses primary ciliogenesis and removal of OFD1 by autophagy promotes it (PMID: 24089205).
Localisation: Distal end of centrioles, centriolar satellites, nucleus

Curator's Note: Also called HNF6. Transcription factor that controls the expression of a network of genes involved in ciliogenesis, cilium function and in hereditary polycystic diseases (PMID: 16472605).
Encodes photoreceptor opsins and is associated with blue cone monochromacy (PMID: 30614359). Requires IFT20 for localisation (PMID: 21307337).
Encodes photoreceptor opsins and is associated with blue cone monochromacy (PMID: 30614359). Requires IFT20 for localisation (PMID: 21307337).
Encodes photoreceptor opsins and is associated with blue cone monochromacy (PMID: 30614359). Requires IFT20 for localisation (PMID: 21307337).

Mutations are associated with Seckel syndrome and/or Meier-Gorlin syndrome (PMID: 23516378). Knockdown affects ciliogenesis and Hh signaling. It prevents reduplication events that could lead to supernumerary centrioles, which has been associated with cilia defects (PMID: 30696958).
Neuronal ciliary GPCR
Localisation: Neuronal cilia membrane, base of primary cilia

Curator's Note: Interacts with Rib72, FAP252, and FAP20 to regulate ciliary motility (PMID: 27770595). Required for proper activation of dynein-driven microtubule sliding and for the assembly of regulatory components. Mutations lead to reduced assembly of inner-arm dynein IDA b, the beak-MIP structures and cause severe motility defects (PMID: 31116684).

Description: protein kinase C and casein kinase substrate in neurons 2(PACSIN2)
Curator's Note: Promotes mother centriole to basal body transition at early stages in ciliogenesis. Required for the establishment of an extracellular membrane channel, through interaction with EHD1 to form the membrane tubules that connect the developing cilium to the cell surface. Regulates actin and microtubule cytoskeleton assembly (PMID: 30683896). Modulates primary cilium length in kidney epithelial cells and contributes to normal kidney tubular development/structure and repair (PMID: 23235565).
Localisation: Preciliary membrane during ciliogenesis, Ciliary pocket membrane in mature cilia

Description: platelet activating factor acetylhydrolase 1b regulatory subunit 1(PAFAH1B1)
Curator's Note: Also known as LIS1. It may regulate outer dynein arm activity and ciliary beating in the trachea. Essential role in cytoplasmic dynein regulation, mitosis and neuronal migration. Interacts with NudC(PMID: 17314247). Regulator of cytoplasmic dynein and alters its microtubule-binding affinity (PMID: 22855525).
Localisation: Motile cilium axoneme, basal body and punctate structures throughout the cytoplasmic microtubule network

Description: par-6 family cell polarity regulator alpha(PARD6A)
Curator's Note: Interacts with Par3 and aPKC to form a polarity complex that regulates the stability of the ciliary axoneme (PMID: 15324661)

Also called C2ORF71. Predominantly expressed in the retina. Important for photoreceptor outer segment morphogenesis and visual function in zebrafish (PMID: 29946172). Interacts with WASF3 and recruits it to the primary cilium; coexpression results in expansion of the ciliary tip (PMID: 32312818). Mutations are associated with retinitis pigmentosa (PMID: 20398886)

Centriolar satellite protein/component that serves as a scaffold to target proteins to centrosome during centrosome maturation. When phosphorylated, it recruits Plk1 to the pericentriolar matrix before mitotic entry (PMID: 23345402). Involved in the formation of primary cilia by associating with CEP290 and BBSome during the ciliogenesis: required for ciliary localisation of Rab8. Role in the recruitment of major centrosomal proteins required for the formation of the non-motile primary cilium (PMID: 18772192, PMID: 31023719). Depletion reduces ciliogenesis (PMID: 21985783). Its localisation is dependent on BBS4, mislocalisation leads to deanchoring of centrosomal microtubules (PMID: 15107855). Required for focal ciliary integrity (PMID: 33214552)
Catabolizes cAMP, located in renal primary cilia. Component of the AKAP150 complex, it promotes the hydrolysis of cAMP to negatively regulate cAMP signaling (PMID: 21670265).

Also known as RP43. Mutations have been associated with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa (PMID: 26321862, PMID: 29118501), and increase intracellular cGMP triggering cell death most likely through a calcium/sodium imbalance (PMID: 30998820).
Localisation: Rod photoreceptor outer segment peripheral membrane

Curator's Note: Also known as RP40. Mutations have been associated with autosomal recessive rod-cone dystrophy and increase intracellular cGMP triggering cell death most likely through a calcium/sodium imbalance (PMID: 30998820, PMID: 27588261).
Localisation: Rod photoreceptor outer segment peripheral membrane

Curator's Note: Localised to rod outer segment by ARL13B (PMID: 30573647). Encodes for the inhibitory γ subunit of rod photoreceptor cyclic GMP- phosphodiesterase. Mutations are associated with retinitis pigmentosa (PMID: 20655036).

Retinal disease modifier in patients with digenic Usher syndrome. Homolog of whirlin (USH2D) and harmonin (USH1C). Part of the Usher protein complex (PMID: 20440071). It positions and stabilises GPR98 (PMID: 23055499).
Localisation: Basal body and perinuclear region; ankle-link region of stereocilia.

Curator's Note: Also known as CEP90. Centriolar satelite protein required for centrosome protein recruitment, centrosomal accumulation of PCM-1 and primary cilia formation, as well as BBS4 recruitment and localisation to the cilium (PMID: 23110211). Mutations have been identified as cause of the ciliopathies Joubert and Jeune syndromes (PMID: 26167768).
PIK3AP1, aslo known as BCAP. Centriolar satellite protein that plays a role as negative regulator of ciliogenesis, specifically initiation (PMID: 28775150).

Description: phosphatidylinositol-4- phosphate 3-kinase catalytic subunit type 2 alpha
Curator's Note: Mutations cause syndromic short stature, skeletal abnormalities, and cataracts associated with ciliary dysfunction (PMID: 31034465). Critical for the formation of cilia and for receptor mediated endocytosis. Promotes the activation and pericentriolar localisation of Rab11+ vesicles, triggers the Rab8- dependent pathway and translocation of Smo to the primary cilium. Controls the production of PtdIns3P at the endocytic recycling compartment located at the base of the primary cilium (PMID: 24697898). PI3KC2α- dependent and VPS34- independent generation of PI3P controls primary cilium- mediated autophagy in response to shear stress
Localisation: Perinuclear area, Pericentriolar recycling compartment around the ciliary base

Curator's Note: Also known as VPS15. Interacts with the golgin GM130 to form a complex and ensure efficient loading of IFT20 in vesicles addressed from the cis-Golgi and transported to the basal body of the cilium (PMID: 27882921).

Description: protein kinase cAMP-activated catalytic subunit alpha(PRKACA)
Curator's Note: Catalytic subunit of PKA. At centriolar satellites. Part of a multimeric complex nucleated by PCM1. Phosphorylates NEK10 for CHIP-mediated ubiquitination and proteolysis resulting in cilia resorption. Patched1-ArhGAP36-PKA- Inversin axis determines the ciliary translocation of Smoothened for Sonic Hedgehog pathway activation. PMID: 30598432

Description: protein kinase cAMP-activated catalytic subunit gamma(PRKACG)
Curator's Note: Catalytic subunit of PKA. At centriolar satellites. Part of a multimeric complex nucleated by PCM1. Phosphorylates NEK10 for CHIP-mediated ubiquitination and proteolysis resulting in cilia resorption. Patched1-ArhGAP36-PKA- Inversin axis determines the ciliary translocation of Smoothened for Sonic Hedgehog pathway activation. PMID: 30598432

Description: polycystin 1 like 1, transient receptor potential channel interacting(PKD1L1)
Curator's Note: Interacts with Pkd2 to form a complex that functions as the nodal flow sensor in the motile cilia. This interaction is required for left-right patterning (PMID: 21307098, PMID: 21307093)

Description: polycystin 2, transient receptor potential cation channel(PKD2)
Curator's Note: Also known as PC2. Mutation causes autosomal dominant PKD. Dimerizes with PKD1 to form a channel in the ciliary membrane (PMID: 20392267) and mediate transduction of an extracellular mechanical stimulus into a Ca2+ signaling response involved in the differentiation of kidney tubular epithelial cells (PMID: 12514735, PMID: 26788466). PC2 enhances calcium release from the ER by stimulating the activity of the IP3 receptor (PMID: 26788466). Required for the asymmetric localization of Vangl2 and involved in the

Description: polycystin 2 like 1, transient receptor potential cation channel(PKD2L1)
Curator's Note: PKD1L1-PKD2L1 acts as a ciliary calcium channel controlling ciliary calcium concentration and thereby modifying SMO-activated GLI2 translocation and GLI1 expression (PMID: 24336288). Plays a role in localization with β2- adrenergic receptor (β2AR) on the neuronal primary cilia (PMID: 29230552).

Description: polycystic kidney and hepatic disease 1 (autosomal recessive)(PKHD1)
Curator's Note: Also known as FPC. Functional and/or structural component of primary cilia in kidney tubular cells (PMID: 14978161). Mutations are involved in utosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (PMID: 15458427, PMID: 11898128, PMID: 14983006). PKHD1 may associate with a common pathway that alters ciliary function and cation channel activity and may act as an intraflagellar motor-binding protein. It also interacts with polycystins, which suggest it could be directly or indirectly involved in a common cystogenic pathway (PMID: 14983006).

Regulates of centrosome maturation. Induces the phosphorylation of the transition zone protein nephrocystin-1 and modulates trafficking required for ciliary maintenance or disassembly (PMID: 22701722). Interacts with and activates histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) to promote ciliary deacetylation and resorption. Plk1 is recruited to the pericentriolar region by PCM1 (PMID: 23345402).

Role in pericentrosomal localisation and integrity of centriolar satellite and ciliogenesis through PCM1 phosphorylation (PMID: 26755742). Interacts with CEP78. Over-expression induces centrosome amplification, which prevents the formation of basal bodies leading to loss of primary cilia (PMID: 26701933, PMID: 27246242).

Stable component of centrioles that and plays a role in their formation and maintenance. Mutations cause ciliogenesis defects and impared mitosis, as well as primordial dwarfism (PMID: 26336158, PMID: 23015594, PMID: 22840364).
Localisation: Inner luminal walls and proximal ends of centrioles in the basal body.

Curator's Note: Essential for assembling the distal half of the centriole and the elongation of the centrioles. Mutations of POC5 alter its subcellular localization and induce ciliary retraction (PMID: 19349582), in addition, impair cell cycle, cilia length and centrosome protein interactions (PMID: 30845169 ).
Hydrocephalus and infertility due to dysfunctional motile cilia, cerebellar dysplasia in KO mouse PMID: 21746835

Ciliogenesis is reciprocally regulated by PPARA and NR1H4/FXR through controlling autophagy in vitro and in vivo. Regulates autophagy by controlling transcription of genes involved in autophagic pathways, and activation of PPARA facilitated ciliogenesis independently of cellular nutritional states by activating autophagy (PMID: 29771182).
PP5 interacts with and directly dephosphorylates Dvl2. Overexpression enhaces ciliogenesis (PMID: 29426949).

Interacts with and inhibits Dynamin 2 to induce neuronal ciliogenesis. Forms a complex with the GTPase Dynamin 2 and thereby inhibits its GTPase activity. Mutations of the PQBP1 WW domain cause recessive X-linked intellectual disability (PMID: 23994472).

Antioxidant protein, involved in in the regulation of cilium disassembly (PMID: 24480440) and decreases the activity of Aurora A, through the regulation of the critical NEDD9-Aurora A-HDAC6 signal axis (PMID: 32357862).
Localisation: Not reported in human cells. Flagella and basal bodies of Dunaliella salina

Curator's Note: Also known as PK2. Planar cell polarity core component involved in the development and function of motile cilia (PMID: 24708399). Role in anterograde transport. Required for basal body and cilia orientation (PMID: 24938409).
Also known as PK3. Required for γ-tubulin and Nedd1 recruitment to the basal body, necessary for basal body organization and cilia growth. Pk3 knockdown inhibites ciliogenesis (PMID: 27062996).

Controls recruitment of ciliary membrane components, histone deacetylase, and transcription factors in stem cells. Mutations cause various human retinal disorders by disrupting the cilium‐derived photoreceptor outer segment (PMID: 30523147).
Localisation: Nucleus, rods and cones outer segments

Curator's Note: Mutated in autosomal dominant RP type 60. Splicing factor implicated in the correct splicing of transcripts encoding proteins important for ciliogenesis (PMID: 26167768).
Localisation: Basal body, apical inner segment, apical connecting cilium of photoreceptor cells, nuclear speckles

Curator's Note: Mutated in autosomal dominant RP type 13. Splicing factor implicated in the correct splicing of transcripts encoding proteins important for ciliogenesis. It has been implicated in the process of centriolar under-duplication (PMID: 26167768).
Localisation: Basal body, apical inner segment, apical connecting cilium of photoreceptor cells, nuclear speckles

Curator's Note: Photoreceptor-specific tetraspanin protein, essential for the morphogenesis of the outer segment (PMID: 30819798). Role in generating and/or sensing the curvature associated with creation and maintenance of OS membrane architecture (PMID: 23886945). Mutations are associated with RP (PMID: 25805137).
Localisation: Outer segment disk membranes, Luminal side of the late endosome

Curator's Note: Also known as EP4. Activates cAMP-mediated signaling cascade. Together with COX- 2, is required for cilia formation and elongation. Increases the intracellular cAMP and activates protein kinase A (PKA) signaling (PMID: 25173977).

Interacts with both basal bodies and actin; its downregulation leads to defects in ciliogenesis (PMID: 24434137). It is a regulator of the actin cytoskeleton, cell adhesion, migration and plays a scaffolding role in multiciliated cells (PMID: 27895123).

Involved in centrosomal duplication, cytokinesis, and plays a role in ciliary length determination (PMID: 19284988, PMID: 21289087). Depletion may lengthen cilia and accumulate higher levels of Gli3 via increased anterograde transport (PMID: 21289087).
Ciliary GPCR

Negative regulator of ciliogenesis. Rab10 phosphorylation enhances binding to RILPL1, which in turn strengthens its ability to block ciliogenesis (PMID: 30398148). Mediates membrane protein trafficking (PMID: 21856246). Interacts in a protein complex with Sec8 at the basal body (PMID: 20576682).
Localisation: Centrosome, pericentriolar membranes. Basal body of nascent cilia.

Curator's Note: Regulator of the endocytic recycling compartment (ERC), binds to Rabin8 and transport it to the centrosome where it activates Rab8 to assemble the ciliary membrane from the ciliary vesicle (PMID: 20308558, PMID: 31204173, PMID: 22718902). Rabin8- Rab11a interaction and preciliary trafficking are promoted by PI3K and Akt inhibitors (PMID: 31204173).
Involved in membrane trafficking, necessary for ciliogenesis (PMID: 17646400). Involved in the function of apical sorting endosomes in polarized epithelial cells (PMID: 9490718)

Negative regulator of the Hedgehog signaling pathway, required for retrograde transport away from primary cilia (PMID: 17646400). It mediates the ciliary recycle of Smo (PMID: 20375059). Facilitates binding of cytiplasmatic Kif17 with ciliary import carrier importin β2, essential for its targeting to the primary cilium (PMID: 26136363).

Colocalizes and interacts with Rab8, Rab11 and IFT20. Participates in ciliogenesis by controlling cilium growth, by promoting the transport of endosome-associated ciliary cargo to the base of the cilium. Required for Smo trafficking to the ciliary membrane.
Localisation: Cis-golgi, trans-Golgi network, base of cilium

Curator's Note: Also known as Rabin8. GTP loading by Rabin8 promotes Rab8 association with post- Golgi vesicles and targets them to polarised areas of the plasma membrane. BBS1 subunit of the BBSome associates with the C terminus of Rabin8 at the basal body. Activates Rab8 by loading with GTP, which is necessary for Rab8 to enter the primary cilium, promoting ciliogenesis and apical membrane formation (PMID: 17574030). Phosphorylation of Rabin8 might modulate its interactions with ASAP1 and Rab11a. It binds to the catalytically active ASAP1 in complex with Rab11a and FIP3 (PMID: 25673879). Interacts with Chibby to promote recruitment of Rab8 and efficient assembly of ciliary vesicles. Interaction with Rab11 stimulates its GEF activity (PMID: 25313408)

Rab34 regulates the early steps in serum starvation- induced ciliogenesis in hTERT-RPE1 cells, through a unique N-terminal region, by regulating the ciliary vesicle fusion step and/or the subsequent expansion. Required for ciliogenesis in only certain cell types (PMID: 32669361). Rab34 is required for the successive fusion of small preciliary vesicles in order to generate ciliary vesicles, it is also required for the migration of the mother centriole from perinuclear region to cell membrane. Required for an early step of ciliary vesicle formation and Hh signaling in vivo. Mutation results in significant decrease of ciliogenesis in both cultured cells and mice (PMID: 30301781). Potential transcriptional target of Gli transcription factors (PMID: 17442700).

Rab8 targets vesicles to the cilium and promotes ciliary membrane elongation. It is activated by Rabin8 (PMID: 17574030, PMID: 22433857). Inactivating Rab8 (GDP- bound state) blocks ciliogenesis and induces BBS phenotypes in zebrafish (PMID: 17574030). Rab8a, Rab8b and Rab10 work synergistically for ciliogenesis (PMID: 24213529). Description: rabaptin, RAB GTPase binding effector protein 2(RABEP2)
Curator's Note: RABEP2 localization at the centrosome is regulated by SDCCAG8. As a component of cilium, it may be a component of the intraciliary transport mechanism. siRNA mediated knockdown in hTERT-RPE1 cells abolished cilia formation, indicating a critical role in ciliogenesis (PMID: 27224062).

Description: RAB, member of RAS oncogene family-like 2A(RABL2A)
Curator's Note: RABL2 paralog. Functionally redundant with RABL2B as they can rescue ciliogenesis when both genes have been knocked out (PMID: 28625565). Associates with ciliary GPCR in mammalian primary cilia and regulates theirs localisation (PMID: 30578315). Two variants in RABL2A were identified as cause of male infertility and ciliopathy (PMID: 33075816). RABL2 might play a role in trafficking of ciliary proteins as well as ciliogenesis. RABL2A/B knock out lead to decrease in number of primary cilia in RPE1 cells (PMID: 30578315).

Ran GTP regulates ciliary protein transport and ciliogenesis (PMID: 21998203). RanGTP gradient regulates trafficking and entry of kinesin motor KIF17 into cilium. It has been proposed that Ran plays a role in regulating cellular compartmentalisation by controlling the shuttling of cytoplasmic proteins into ciliary compartments (PMID: 20526328). Interacts with Importin β2, which interacts directly with cargoes, releasing them upon binding Ran GTP and regulating localisation of RP2 (PMID: 21285245).

Negative regulator of calcineurin and modulates Ca2+ dependent signalling. Required to maintain normal cilia length. Depletion in WT RPE-1 cells results in shorter cilia, whilst in giantin KO cells induces longer cilia (PMID: 29643119).

Also known as CAPZIP. Ortholog duboraya (dub), has been reported to be essential for actin organization in the cells lining Kupffer's vesicle, regulates ciliogenesis in a phosphorylation-dependent manner as well as left-right patterning in zebrafish (PMID: 17013396). Phosphorylated by ERK7. Ciliogenesis regulations through CapZIP, requires Dvl binding to both ERK7 and CapZIP (PMID: 25823377).

Involved in regulation of ALMS1 in vivo, by binding its promoter (PMID: 20381594). Coordinates multiple, distinct gene expression programs in MCCs, regulating genes encoding axonemal dynein subunits, components of the transition zone anb BBSome, centriolar genes and planar cell polarity (PCP) effector fritz/wdpcp. It also regulates the extracellular matrix component dag1, which is a

Transcription factor regulating expression of ciliary assembly (like Dync2li1, Foxj1 and Bbs4) and axonemal dyneins involved in ciliary motility (Dnahc11, Dnahc9 and Dnahc5), by binding directly to the promoters of their genes. Regulates the orthologs of genes involved inhuman PCD. It may also cooperate with FOXJ1 to regulate the expression of cilia genes (PMID: 19671664). Regulates the expression of D2lic in mouse, a gene implicated in intraflagellar transport, a proces required for the assembly and maintenance of cilia. RFX3 is essential for the differentiation of nodal monocilia and for LR patterning (PMID: 15121860). Together with FOXJ1, plays a role in modulating differentiation in multiciliated cells (PMID: 23822649).

Modulates Shh signaling and and Gli3 processing by regional control of ciliogenesis and function of primary cilia. Rfx4 nuclear translocation and/or transcriptional activity, may be regulated by phosphorylation. Required for ciliogenesis in the neural tube (PMID: 19887680). It appears to regulate different genes than RFX3, as Rfx4 KO embryos exhibite different
Highly expressed in Brain. RFX7 controls positively the formation of cilia by regulating the expression of RFX4 gene. Involved in complete neural tube closure (PMID: 24530844).

Cilia-specific GPCR essential for vision. Multiple roles in trafficking, interacts with Arf4, TcTex-1 and SARA (PMID: 23966685). Mutations cause protein misfolding and retention in the endoplasmic reticulum, leading to cellular stress and cell death. Mutations are associated with retinitis pigmentosa (PMID: 32343782).

Rab effector-related protein, regulates protein concentration by removal of membrane proteins from the cilium. Depletion results in accumulation of signaling proteins in the ciliary membrane, including Smo. Interacts with activated Rab34, Rab36, Rab12 and Rab40B (PMID: 23264467). Interacts with the LRRK2- phosphorylated forms of Rab8A and Rab10 (PMID: 29125462). Enhances pRab10 clustering on pericentriolar membranes to
Localisation: Cilium, Basal Body (distal end of mother centriole)

Curator's Note: Rab effector-related protein that exhibist dynamic localisation; regulates protein concentration by removal of membrane proteins from the cilium.. Depletion results in accumulation of signaling proteins in the ciliary membrane, including Smo. Interacts with activated Rab34 and Rab36 (PMID: 23264467). Binds to phosphorylated Rab8A, Rab10, and Rab12. As it binds Rab8a much stronger than RILPL1, RILPL2 might be a key effector specific for pRab8A (PMID: 29125462).

Description: RHO family interacting cell polarization regulator 2(RIPOR2)
Curator's Note: Mutations cause deafness. Interacts with Myh9, which is related to deafness. Regulates the abundance and post translational modifications of proteins highly expressed within the kinocilium , which suggestes a role in hair bundle morphogenesis (PMID: 30280293).

Outer segment protein. Its localisation depends on AHI1 (PMID: 20592197). Non- covalently linked PRPH2/ROM1 complex can initiate OS formation, whilst covalent oligomerisation is required for proper OS maturation (PMID: 32716032, PMID: 29961824). Creates and maintains the rim region
Functions as a key molecule in the maintenance of basal ciliary beat frequency. Its role in ciliary motility coulb be played via regulation of axonemal signaling (PMID: 22021175)

Nonsense mutation associated with retinitis pigmentosa (PMID: 10401003). Microtubule- associated protein containing the doublecortin (DCX) domain. Disruption of Rp1 in mice causes misorientation of outer segment discs, suggesting a role in outer segment organisation. Stimulates microtubule polymerization and stabilise existing microtubules in vitro and in vivo, therefore, it controls the length and stability of the photoreceptor axoneme (PMID: 15269252). Due to Rp1 localisation, it may be involved in the formation of outer segments (PMID: 11773008). Plays synergistic role with Rp1L1 in affecting photosensitivity and OS morphogenesis of rod photoreceptors (PMID: 19657028).
Localisation: Connecting Cilium and outer segment portion of photoreceptor axoneme.

Curator's Note: Interacts with Arl3 and mediates the localization of GFP-Kif17 to the cilia tip and interacts with the regulator of Hedgehog (Hh) signaling Kif7. This suggests RP2 is implicated primary cilia protein trafficking via the regulation of kinesin motor proteins at the ciliary tip (PMID: 28444310). Loss of RP2 leads to fragmentation of the Golgi network and dispersal of vesicles cycling cargo from the Golgi complex to the cilium, including IFT20. It indicates a role for RP2 in regulating vesicle traffic and docking from the Golgi to the base of the cilium (PMID: 20106869). Interacts with polycystin 2 and regulates its trafficking within the cilium (PMID: 20729296). RP2 entry to the ciliary compartiment is regulated by Importin β2 (PMID: 21285245). Mutations are associated with with X- linked retinitis pigmentosa (PMID: 9697692).
Localisation: Golgi, Basal Body and along the length of the ciliary compartment

Description: retinitis pigmentosa GTPase regulator interacting protein 1(RPGRIP1)
Curator's Note: Known ciliopathy gene CORD13. Mutations are known causes of RP and Leber congenital amaurosis. Potential structural component of the ciliary axoneme, which anchors RPGR within the cilium (PMID: 11104772, PMID: 15772089). Required for disk morphogenesis and RPGR retention in the connecting cilium (PMID: 12651948). Essential for rod OS formation, probably by regulating the transport of proteins from the IS to the OS (PMID: 19679561). Required for ciliary targeting of NPHP4 and SDCCAG8, Rab8 localisation in photoreceptors and is involved in rhodopsin ciliary vesicle transport in zebrafish (PMID: 29203866).

Localizes to centrosomes, cilia and nucleoli. Highly expressed in neural stem cells in developing human forebrain, and a missense mutation is associated with microcephaly. Targeted mutation of Rrp7a leads to defects in neurogenesis and proliferation in a mouse stem cell model and in zebrafish causes reduced brain size, impaired neurogenesis and cell proliferation, and defective ribosomal RNA processing. Patient-derived fibroblasts display defects in

Mutations have been shown to cause PCD (PMID: 25473808, PMID: 24568568). Integral component of the ciliary axoneme expressed during ciliated cell differentiation (PMID: 24568568). Mainly expressed in tissues with motile cilia or flagella; absence of RSPH1 leads toabnormal axonemal configuration with central- complex defects, suggesting a role for RSPH1 in proper building of central-complexes and radial spokes (PMID: 23993197).
Localisation: Cilium, axoneme, radial spoke region of the sperm flagellum

Curator's Note: Protein kinase A-anchoring protein that scaffolds the cAMP-dependent protein kinase holoenzyme (PMID: 19684019). Mutations are associated with PCD, with CC/RS defects like abnormal axoneme configuration and absence of RS. Required for proper building of RSs and the CC in humans (PMID: 26073779). Mutations in RSPH3 in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii lead to paralyzed flagella due to loss of the entire radial spoke structure (PMID: 29475374).

RSPH6A is required for sperm flagellar assembly and male fertility in mice. Interacts with RSPH1, RSPH4A, RSPH9 and RSPH10B, where nteraction of RSPH6A and RSPH9 is important to incorporate RSPH9 into the flagella. Absence of RSPH6A leads to immotile spermatozoa in mice (PMID: 30185526). Expressed exclusively in testicular germ cells during meiosis. Rsph6a is phosphorylated by PKA during sperm capacitation (PMID: 30239614).
Localisation: Radial spoke of motile cilium, flagellar axoneme.

Curator's Note: Component of the axonemal radial spoke head. Mutations cause PCD with defects of the central microtubular pair, where altered function of the radial spoke heads causes 9+2 cilia motility to resemble the rotary 9+0 cilia movement (PMID: 19200523). Essential for ciliary structure and motility in mouse ependymal cilia; deletion causes hydrocephalus. Dysfunction of RSPH9 changes the motion pattern of motile cilia. (PMID: 32709945). Required for RS

Regulates early embryonic axial rotation, anteroposterior and dorsoventral patterning in mice and is required for maintenance of a normal ciliary structure (PMID: 22939636). Required for assembly of full-length centrioles through its STIL- RTTN interaction; it also serves as an upstream effector of CEP295 (PMID: 28811500). Centrosomal protein possibly involved in centriolar elongation and ciliogenesis. Mutations cause polymicrogyria (PMID: 30879067) and missense or splicing variants have been found in patients with microcephaly (PMID: 29967526).

Role in the pre-assembly and targeting of ciliary protein complexes. Ruvbl1 may be a major organiser of dynein arm complex assembly (PMID: 29959317). Essential for cilia motility in both zebrafish and mouse, cooperating with Ruvbl2 through the assembly of ciliary ODAs and IDAs; requires Ruvbl2 for stability. Essential for the stabilization of axonemal dynein intermediate chain 1 (DNAI1) and DNAI2 in mouse,and facilitates dynein arm assembly in cytosolic foci enriched with R2TP-like complexes (PMID:

Essential for cilia motility in both zebrafish and mouse, through the assembly of ciliary ODAs and IDAs and cooperating with Ruvbl1. Interacts with Hsp90 to regulate the stability of both DNAI1 and DNAI2. Requires Ruvbl1 for stability (PMID: 29113992). Involved in epigenetic and transcriptional regulation of cilia motility genes; interacts with LRRC6 in a complex involved in dynein arm formation, essential for cilia motility in zebrafish. Candidate gene for PCD (PMID: 23858445).

Zinc-finger transcription factor that mediates transcriptional repression via its interaction with the nucleosome- remodeling deacetylase (NuRD) complex. Truncated SALL1 interacts with or sequester factors related to cilia function, including the negative regulators of ciliogenesis CCP110 and CEP97. SALL1 mutations can disrupt cilia formation and function (PMID: 29395072). Truncated SALL1 increases the ubiquitin proteasome- mediated degradation of LUZP1, contributing to Townes-Brocks Syndrome (PMID: 32553112).

FAM154A. A microtubule- stabilizing protein specific to cilia and related structures. Regulates cilium axonemal length and promotes microtubule assembly in Hela , RPE1 cells and Trypanosome Brucei (PMID: 33200789). It binds specifically to centriole and cilium microtubules and is responsible for their targeting and stabilisation. SAXO1 is also reported to be present across the length of human sperm flagellum where it colocalizes with α-tubulin, where it could play a role in its biogenesis, stability and length (PMID: 25673876)

Description: S-phase cyclin A associated protein in the ER(SCAPER)
Curator's Note: Varians have been associated with intellectual disability and autosomal recessive RP. Mutations affect cilia length, suggesting a rol for SCAPER in restricting cilia elongation or enhancing cilia resorption (PMID: 30723319). Although it is ubiquitously expressed in human tissues, deleterious mutations appear to affect

Recruited to centrioles via CEP83. Subsequently, it recruits FBF1 and CEP164. Depletion of SCLT1 in RPE1 cells disruptes CEP164 localisation and blockes cilia formation (PMID: 23348840). Variants have been identified in patients with a severe ciliopathy phenotype. Candidate gene of autosomal recessive Oro‐Facio‐Digital (OFD) syndrome (PMID: 24285566). Recruits LRRC45 to the distal appendages of mother centriole (PMID: 30131441).

Mutations cause nephronophthisis type 10. Interacts with ODF1 and FAM161A (PMID: 20835237, PMID: 24722439) and FA161A; plays a role in intraciliary trafficking and is essential for the survival and maintenance of both rods and cones (PMID: 24722439). Mutations have also been reported in patients with Bardet-Biedl syndrome (PMID: 22190896). Required for the formation of outer segments (PMID: 22825473).
Localisation: Basal Body, Centrioles, Transition Zone, connecting cilium

Curator's Note: Component of a diffusion barrier at the ciliary base, essential for retaining receptor-signaling pathways in the primary cilium, and is required for cilium-dependent Shh signal transduction. Depletion inhibits ciliogenesis (PMID: 20558667). Ciliary localisation of SEPT2, suggest that it is involved in organization of the axonemal microtubular structure, controling ciliogenesis and ciliary length (PMID: 24317785). Forms a complex with SEPT7 and SEPT9 to positively control ciliogenesis and the length of cilia (PMID: 23572511).

Associates with acetylated α- tubulin and controls ciliogenesis. Knockdown results in aberrant cilium formation. Required for left- right patterning of visceral organs in zebrafish by controlling nodal signaling and through KV ciliogenesis. Sept6 is also required for ciliogenesis in the neural tube (PMID: 24469395).

Binds to Ptc1 and inactivates it, leading to accumulation of Smo and activation of signaling. Primary cilia regulates its activity (PMID: 17641202). Shh controls patterning and proliferation through the primary cilium (PMID: 31825820).

Shh signaling maintains Siah2 expression (which supports ciliogenesis in a feed-forward fashion by restraining cilium disassembly) in cerebellar granule neuron (CGN) progenitors (GNPs) in a Ras/Mapk-dependent manner. This maintains GNPs to control CGN occupancy in the germinal zone (GZ) (PMID: 33082319)

Regulates cell cycle progression at mitosis, replication and G1/S transition. SIRT2 acts as a sensor that links growth factor-dependent signal transduction and primary cilia formation by regulating the cell cycle under nutrient- present conditions. Suppression leads to a cell cycle arrest and promotes formation of primary cilia, by inhibiting mTOR signaling mainly via mTORC1 (PMID: 32213867). Functions as a tubulin deacetylase. Regulates ciliogenesis and centrosome amplification. Inhibition of SIRT2 induces hyperacetylation of α-tubulin and blocks cilia dissaembly. SIRT2 could also be responsible for aberrant centrosome amplification and polyploidy in polycystic kidney disease (PMID: 24203696).

Also known as MATE2. It is a multidrug and toxin extrusion transporter as well as transportes of other positively charged small molecules, and a brain-specific central gene in the ciliary module (PMID: 22558177).

Also known as EBP50 or NHERF1. Regulates Wnt and PCP signaling PCP signaling and the development of functional motile cilia via binding the planar cell polarity genes Frizzled (Fzd) and Vangl. Knockdown in zebrafish embryos causes severe hydrocephalus. Ablation causes reduced number and altered orientation of the cilia but does not change the structural organization of the cilium (PMID: 27055101).

Madiator in the activation of TGF-β signaling pathway and controls cilia length (PMID: 25959824). Downstream of TGFBR1 and 2, which phosphorylate SMAD2/3 at base of cilium upon TGF-β stimulation (PMID: 23746451).

Translocates to the primary cilium membrane and activates downstream signaling. It is enriched in cilia upon stimulation with Shh (PMID: 17641202). Smo traslocation to the cilium results in Glis activation (PMID: 28344083). Hh signalling depends upon a Smo ciliary localization (PMID: 16136078). Defect in Smo localisation results from defective retrograde transport (PMID: 16229832). For instance, defects in intraflagellar transport components Ift27 and the BBSome, cause ciliary accumulation of Smo without pathway activation (PMID: 32435793).

Regulate rhodopsin delivery; controls ciliogenesis through the expansion of the ciliary membrane and rod outer segments biogenesis (PMID: 19454479). Potentially involved in membrane trafficking into the outer segment (PMID: 9452464).
Localisation: Cilium, ciliary membrane, base of cilium.

Curator's Note: Required for the formation of primary cilia and essential for left-right patterning of visceral organs. Binds to V-ATPase to regulate its centrosomal trafficking and Rab8a vesicle trafficking to the ciliary membrane. Those events are crucial for ciliogenesis (PMID: 21844891).

SNX17 functions in early stages of ciliogenesis. Regulates the homeostasis of centriolar satellite proteins including PCM1, CEP131, and OFD1 during serum starvation induced ciliogenesis. Recruits USP9X to antagonise MIB1-induced degradation of PCM1, maintaining the integrity of centriolar satellites. SNX17 deficiency leads degradation of USP9X and PCM1, and disrupts ciliogenesis upon serum starvation (PMID: 31671755).

Regulatory role in a PKA- independent AKAP complex in both germinal cells and somatic ciliated epithelia. It may also play a role in cell motility (PMID: 19604394, PMID: 15034007). Binds the RII binding domain of AKAP3 along the length of the flagella (PMID: 15257753).

Orthologue of Chlamydomonas reinhardtii PF20, known to be essential to the structure and function of the motile axoneme. Encodes two proteins, SPAG16L and SPAG16S. SPAG16L is essential for sperm flagellar motility. Interacts with SPAG6, which in turn interacts with SPAG17. Mutation results in instability of interacting proteins in the central pair of the sperm axoneme. (PMID: 16382026, PMID: 17699735). SPAG16S, identified only in male germ cells, plays a role in the gene expression machinery of male germ cells required for spermatogenesis, and it also modulates Spag16L mRNA expression (PMID: 21655194). Transcription of SPAG16 is regulated through S-SOX5 binding to the promoter (PMID: 28137312).
Localisation: Cytoplasm, central apparatus of the axoneme (SPAG16L), nuclear speckles (SPAG16S).

Curator's Note: Encodes a central pair protein present motile cilia or flagella with a ‘9+2’ axoneme structure and plays both a structural and functional role in the ciliary axoneme. Interacts with SPAG6 and SPAG16. KO mice have immotile nasal and tracheal cilia, respiratory problems and hydrocephalus (PMID: 23418344). Essential for proper development of the sperm flagellum and

Orthologue of Chlamydomonas PF16. Axoneme central apparatus protein, essential for sperm flagellar motility and motility of ependymal cilia, as well as maintenance of the structural integrity of the sperm flagella by serving as a scaffold protein (PMID: 12167721). Role in ciliogenesis, axoneme orientation, and cell polarity. Spag6-deficient epithelial cells in the brain and trachea lose rotational polarity and Spag6-eficient mice suffer hydrocephalus and are sterile because of sperm motility defects (PMID: 25333478). Mutated in PCD with male infertility with severe asthenoteratospermia (PMID: 32124190)
Localisation: Axoneme, center of the transition zone at the site of central pair assembly, cytoplasm.

Curator's Note: Expressed in spermatocytes and in the mature retina. Mutations have been associated with Leber Congenital Amaurosis and Retinitis Pigmentosa (PMID: 19268277). Component of a protein complex which interacts with CETN2 and CETN3 to stabilise the photoreceptor distal connecting cilium and proximal OS axoneme (PMID: 30647131). Interacts with photoreceptor-specific ciliary proteins RPGR and RPGRIP1 to maintain distal connecting cilium (DCC) structure; it also
Localisation: Cytoplasm of inner segment of photoreceptors

Curator's Note: Also known as CLAMP. Regulator of PCP signaling, via localisation of asymmetric PCP components and regulates asymmetric microtubule accumulation. Required for proper PCP- dependent establishment of cilia polarity (PMID: 29514918). Microtubule- bundling protein, and central pair MT regulator highly expressed in 9 + 2 mammalian cilia. Essential for the assembly and functions of central pair MTs, central pair apparatus, and for ciliary retentions of other central pair proteins such as Spag6 and Hydin (PMID: 30535028).
Localisation: Axoneme, along central pair, ciliary rootlet

Curator's Note: Essential for correct sperm tail development and male fertility. Interacts with intraflagellar transport protein IFT20. Mutation in SPEF2 was identified as a cause for immotile short tail sperm in pigs (PMID: 19889948). Required for ciliary motility and spermatogenesis. In mouse, loss of SPEF2 function results in PCD with severe spermatogenic defects (PMID: 21715716). Functional defects also lead to PCD due to a defect of the central pair complex. Interacts with HYDIN, which regulates assembly of SPEF2 to the ciliary axoneme, as it cannot
Localisation: Golgi, cytoplasm basal body, midpiece of the sperm tail, sperm manchette, ciliary axoneme

Description: sterol regulatory element binding transcription factor 1(SREBF1)
Curator's Note: Also known as SREBP1. Suppresses primary ciliogenesis. Induces large levels of lysophosphatidylcholine and lysophosphatidylethanolamine , which are typically generated at the outer membrane leaflet. It increases the positive membrane curvature in the plasma membrane and vesicle membranes, causing Rab11- positive vesicles to deviate away from the pericentrosomal preciliary compartment at the ciliary base, suppresing ciliogenesis (PMID: 25904332).

Regulates the actin cytoskeleton, forming a signalling complex with WAVE-1 to regulate its activation. 10% of SrGAP3 knockout mice die from hydrocephalus and display ependymal cells with reduced density of cilia but without alterations in the length (PMID: 26104135).

Ciliary GPCR. Localized to the plasma membrane of neuronal cilia (PMID: 10199624, PMID: 23392690). Ciliary trafficking of SSTR3 into neural cilia is promoted by TULP3. Overexpression induces premature growth of primary cilia and increases expression levels of Kif3A, IFT88 and cytoplasmatic dynein (PMID: 23392690). Possible influence on cell survival and/or apoptotic processes, as well as cell cycle (PMID: 18992731).

Centriolar satellite and microtubule anchoring protein. Interacts with PCM-1. Essential for the assembly of primary cilia and the recruitment of Cep290 to both satellites and the basal body; it also promotes the ciliary entry of the entire BBSome. Knockdown limits targeting of somatostatin receptor 3, and significantly reduces axoneme length. Possible novel cooperator of Rab8 (PMID: 24356449). Binds the microtubule-nucleator γ- tubulin complex. Knockdown of its orthologue in zebrafish, results in ciliary defects and disturbs left-right asymmetry. Microtubule anchoring role to the basal body is required for primary cilia formation (PMID: 24397932).

Downregulated in diseases associated with ciliopathies, including BBS, PKD and PHP. Regulates multiciliogenesis and differenciation of ciliated cells by phosphorylating MARK3 which supresses ERK1/2 (PMID: 31636950). Required for CCL2 regulation within cilia, via interactions with NPHP1, ANKS3 and NEK7 (PMID: 29925518). Bending of cilium activates Lkb1 pathway, which inhibits mTORC1 activity and regulation cell size (PMID: 20972424). Duct-specific deletion causes duct dilations and shorter cilia with swollen tips, indicative of perturbed intraciliary transport (PMID: 28159992).

Phosphorylates Rabin8 which is crucial role in ciliogenesis. Regulates the process of vesicular trafficking and tethering to the pericentrosome, promoting local activation of Rab8 and ciliary membrane formation. Defects in NDR2-mediated Rabin8 phosphorylation impair preciliary membrane assembly and ciliogenesis, leading to accumulation of Rabin8-/Rab11-containing vesicles at the pericentrosome. Knockdown in RPE1 cells suporesses ciliogenesis (PMID: 23435566, PMID: 28122914). Mutated in canine early retinal degeneration, suggesting a role in photoreceptor cell function (PMID: 20887780).

Description: STIP1 homology and U-box containing protein 1(STUB1)
Curator's Note: Also known as CHIP. E3 ub- ligase. Ubiquitylates and degrades NEK10. Novel regulator of protein turnover at ciliary sites, it couples GPCR signaling to cilia dynamics. Downregulation of CHIP prevents cilia resorption whilst increased expression of CHIP is linked to reduced NEK10 levels and ciliogenesis; role in control of cilium stability. Mutations have been reported in patients with autosomal recessive spinocerebellar ataxia-16 SCAR16 (PMID: 29581457 ).

Major partner for SNAP25 in photoreceptor cells and regulates rhodopsin delivery by mediating docking and fusion of rhodopsin transport carriers, expansion of the ciliary membrane and rod outer segments biogenesis (PMID: 19454479). Mislocalises to the outer segment in Bardet-Biedl syndrome (PMID: 31694913, PMID: 26216965).
Localisation: Cilium, base of cilium, plasma membrane of inner segment in photoreceptors.

Description: spectrin repeat containing nuclear envelope protein 1(SYNE1)
Curator's Note: Also known as Nesprin1. Integral components of ciliary rootlets of multiciliated cells. Interacts with rootletin (PMID: 28625779). Essential for the relocalisation of centrosome proteins and components of microtubule motor complexes to the nuclear envelope, and interacts with PCM-1 (PMID: 27802164). Mutations are associated with cerebellar and non-cerebellar pathologies of unknown molecular pathogenesis (PMID: 29630990). Mediates centrosome migration and determinationof centrosome/basal body positioning during early cell polarization, an essential step for ciliogenesis (PMID: 19596800).
Localisation: Ciliary rootlets, nuclear envelope of rod photoreceptors.

Description: spectrin repeat containing nuclear envelope protein 2(SYNE2)
Curator's Note: Also known as Nespirin2. Colocalises with meckelin at filopodia prior to the establishment of cell polarity and ciliogenesis. Mediates centrosome migration and determinationof centrosome/basal body positioning during early cell polarization, an essential step for ciliogenesis. It may form a linking network between the centrosome and the actin cytoskeleton (PMID: 19596800). Role in nuclear

Regulates intracellular protein trafficking and organisation of cellular organelles; it could also play a role in ciliary assembly and signaling. Defective TAPT1 mislocalises to the cytoplasm, disrupts Golgi morphology, trafficking and normal ciliogenesis. Knockdown of tapt1b in zebrafish induces severe malformations of the craniofacial skeleton (PMID: 26365339).

Cytoplasmic retention of YAP/TAZ correlates with active ciliogenesis either in spatially confined cells or in cells treated with an actin filament destabilizer. Moreover, knockdown of YAP/TAZ is sufficient to induce ciliogenesis, whereas YAP/TAZ hyperactivation suppresses serum starvation- mediated ciliogenesis.

PMID:17646400 involved in membrane trafficking, necessary for ciliogenesis (PMID: PMID: 17646400). GAP protein that regulates activity of specific Rab GTPases including RAB3A22 and RAB8A (PMID: 23263489).
GTPase-activating protein that controls specific Rabs involved in primary cilium formation. TBC1D7 specifically acts on Rab17.

Required for centrosome and Golgi apparatus perinuclear positioning. Depletion reduces primary cilia assembly efficiency/ability and affectes cell shape and migration. TBCCD1-silenced cells showed disorganised Golgi apparatus (PMID: 20168327). Candidate for primary cause of centrosome amplification due to gain of function (PMID: 32681070).
Localisation: Centrosome, basal body of primary and motile cilia.

Curator's Note: Dynein-2 light chain, required for cilia function. Associates with WDR34 (PMID: 25205765) and WDR60, which is required for ciliary protein trafficking, as KO cells show defects in retrograde ciliary protein trafficking (PMID: 29742051). Causative gene for short-rib polydactyly syndromes. DFNB31/whirlin. PDZ scaffold protein. Mutated in autosomal recessive non-syndromic deafness type 31 (PMID: 12833159) and Usher syndrome type 2D (PMID:17171570) in humans (OMIM 607928). Only the whirlin long isoform (with an additional N-terminal PDZ domain) is expressed in the retina, the retina is affected if this extra PDZ domain is mutated (PMID: 20502675). Localises to the tiip of the ssterocilium of the cochlear hair cell (PMID: 15590698). Interacts directly with USH2A and VLGR1 in the connecting cilium of photoreceptor cells (PMID: 16434480). Colocalizes with MPP1 in the retina at the outer limiting membrane, at the outer synaptic layer and at the basal bodies and the ciliary axoneme of the connecting cilium of the photoreceptors (PMID: 17584769). Interacts with L-type calcium channel subunit Ca(v)1.3 (alpha(1D) at synpase in retina (PMID: 19959638). Interacts with RPGR(ORF15) in the photoreceptors (PMID: 22323458)
Localisation: Basal body and axoneme of photoreceptor connecting cilium. Outer limiting membrane and outer synaptic layer of retina. Tip of sterocilium of cochlear hair cell.

Curator's Note: Mitochondrial protein expressed specifically in distal convoluted tubule and cortical collecting duct cells. Homozygous frameshift and splice-site mutations cause an autosomal recessive nephronophisis-like nephropathy in humans (OMIM:613553), PMID: 20179356. targeted to mitochondria by an amino- terminal mitochondrial signal sequence. Has N-terminal proline cleavage activity. E.coli ortholog can can efficiently cleave CEP290/NPHP6, ALMS1, and LRRC50 N-terminus. Cleavage of N-terminus of LRRC50 is essential for normal gastrulation in zebrafish (PMID: 20179356)
Localisation: Mitochondria (processed form), cytosol (unprocessed form). Specifically in distal convoluted tubule and cortical collecting duct cells
